Galvanic Myofibril Lash#

The Galvanic Myofibril Lash is a flexible close-combat weapon produced by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, consisting of a 1.8-meter braided cord of synthetic myofibril polymer threaded with a continuous galvanic filament network. When activated, the lash generates a rolling galvanic charge across its entire length, peaking at the tip where contact is most likely. On contact with biological tissue, the charge triggers involuntary myofibril contraction in the target's musculature — not merely painful surface-level stimulation, but a deep galvanic cascade that forces the target's own muscle fibers to seize against themselves, producing acute cramping, postural collapse, and in sustained contact scenarios, localized rhabdomyolysis.

The GML-2's design is informed by Zheng-Dao's extensive proprietary research into synthetic muscle systems for their prosthetics division. The myofibril polymer used in the lash is a byproduct of rejected actuator materials — too brittle for load-bearing prosthetic use but ideal for a flexible weapon that needs to conduct charge without becoming rigid. The polymer gives the lash an unsettling quality in motion: it moves with slightly too much fluid articulation, more like a living appendage than a manufactured cord, and operators who train extensively with it develop an instinctive, almost organic style of combat that observers describe as watching someone fight with a severed limb.

Against cyborg targets, the GML-2 performs inconsistently — heavily augmented individuals with subdermal insulation are largely immune, while those with neural-muscular interface implants can experience catastrophic feedback through the lash's charge interfacing with their augmentation's own signal pathways. Zheng-Dao does not advertise this latter effect.

Galvanic Periosteal Fatigue Emitter GPFE-4 'Hairline'#

The GPFE-4 functions by projecting a pulsed galvanic current through a directed beam of ionized saline vapor, creating a conductive pathway that deposits low-frequency electrical oscillations directly into bone tissue. These oscillations do not fracture bone acutely — instead, they induce accelerated piezoelectric fatigue at the microscopic level, progressively weakening the crystalline hydroxyapatite matrix that gives bone its structural integrity. A single sustained exposure of three to five seconds produces microfractures distributed across the targeted load-bearing bone. The target feels a deep ache but remains mobile. Under any significant mechanical stress — running, jumping, a hard fall — the bone fails catastrophically along the fatigue lines.

The delayed-onset nature of the damage is the weapon's defining and most disturbing characteristic. A target struck by the GPFE-4 may not experience incapacitation for minutes or hours after exposure, during which time they appear entirely functional. The weapon is consequently almost impossible to counter in the moment of use — by the time the injury manifests, the operator is long gone. Helix Biosystems developed the GPFE-4 ostensibly as a research instrument for studying accelerated bone fatigue in microgravity simulation environments. Its migration into weapons applications was unofficial and rapid.

The 'Hairline' nickname reflects both the weapon's mechanism — hairline fractures distributed across bone — and the razor-thin margin it exploits between appearing unharmed and being on the verge of catastrophic skeletal failure. Among GLMZ's medical community, injuries consistent with GPFE-4 exposure are referred to informally as 'slow breaks' or 'time bombs,' and diagnosing them before they manifest requires specialized bone density imaging that most public clinics cannot afford.

Galvanic Vapor Diffusion Pistol GVDP-1 'Saltlick'#

The GVDP-1 generates a cloud of electrostatically charged ionic vapor by flash-vaporizing a saline-metallic solution through a galvanic induction chamber. The resulting mist carries a sustained galvanic charge that, upon contact with biological tissue, drives ions through the skin's surface via electrophoretic pressure — bypassing the need for penetration or direct electrical contact. Once ionic particles have penetrated the skin barrier, they create a localized galvanic circuit within the tissue itself, generating heat and electrochemical disruption at the cellular level. The effect is experienced as a deep burning sensation beneath the skin with no visible external cause, accompanied by involuntary muscle fasciculation.

The GVDP-1's vapor cloud persists for approximately 8-12 seconds in still air before dispersing, during which time any target moving through it receives continuous ionic exposure. This area-denial quality distinguishes it from point-target electrical weapons — the cloud hangs in space and punishes movement through it rather than requiring the operator to track a specific target. In enclosed spaces with limited airflow, the persistence time extends significantly, making interior engagements particularly dangerous. The weapon is largely ineffective outdoors in strong wind, a limitation operators learn to account for.

Ringo Corponation produced the GVDP-1 as part of a broader non-lethal compliance tool line marketed to corporate security divisions and private detention facilities. Its civilian applications — crowd management, perimeter enforcement in enclosed facilities — gave it broad initial distribution before its more aggressive applications became apparent. The pistol form factor makes it concealable, and the vapor it produces is colorless in most lighting conditions, contributing to its reputation as a weapon that creates confusion about the source and nature of the attack.

Gauss Flechette Repeater GFR-3 'Needlerain'#

The GFR-3 operates on stacked linear magnetic acceleration coils arranged in a helical configuration, cycling sub-caliber tungsten-ceramic flechettes at approximately 4,200 rounds per minute. Each flechette — roughly 3mm wide and 22mm long — is ferromagnetically coated along its rear third, allowing the coil stack to grab, accelerate, and release in under 0.8 milliseconds per round. The result is a nearly silent, caseless stream of kinetic penetrators that can saturate a doorframe-sized area at close range or punch through light armor panels at distance.

What distinguishes the GFR-3 from earlier gauss repeaters is its adaptive coil timing system, which reads barrel temperature and magnetic field saturation 200 times per second and adjusts current delivery to maintain consistent muzzle velocity even as the barrel heats. Earlier models suffered from 'velocity drift,' where rounds fired late in a magazine were significantly slower than initial rounds, producing inconsistent terminal performance. The GFR-3 solved this through TESSERA CORPONATION's proprietary FluxSync firmware, which also enables selectable dispersion patterns — tight column for armor penetration, wide fan for crowd suppression.

The weapon uses a 300-round cassette magazine that sits beneath the barrel in a bullpup configuration, giving the GFR-3 a stubby, aggressive silhouette. It has no mechanical action, no ejection port, and minimal moving parts beyond the cassette feed mechanism, which makes it exceptionally reliable in wet or contaminated environments. The lack of a traditional trigger group — replaced by a capacitive palm sensor and a pressure ring around the grip — means the weapon cannot fire if not held correctly, a feature that has made it popular with corporate security who worry about weapon retention.

Its silence — the loudest component is the faint magnetic hum and the impact of flechettes — makes it favored for operations where noise discipline matters. The 300-round cassette allows sustained suppressive fire without reloads, though operators are trained to swap cassettes at 150 rounds to avoid feed jams from heat buildup in the advancement mechanism. Some operators tape two cassettes together for rapid exchange.
cultural context The GFR-3 carries a specific social weight in GLMZ: it is the weapon of the corporate floor. Seen holstered on TESSERA's own lobby security and licensed to a dozen mid-tier corporate clients, the 'Needlerain' is understood as a statement of institutional violence — clean, efficient, calibrated. Street gangs rarely carry them because the cassette magazines are expensive and proprietary. When one appears outside a corporate context, it usually means someone raided a security depot or a corporate operative has gone freelance. The weapon's silence gives it a particular dread reputation in the lower arcologies, where the first sign of a GFR-3 in the room is often the sound of someone else getting hit.

Grave Protocol Arms Entropy Pistol EP-1 'Half Life'#

A compact directed energy weapon that fires a focused beam of accelerated beta particles — essentially a handheld radioactive emitter that delivers a lethal radiation dose to a targeted area. The Half Life produces no visible beam, no sound, and no immediate physical effect. Targets exposed to the beam develop acute radiation syndrome over the following hours to days, with lethality depending on exposure duration.

Grave Protocol Arms — the same phantom manufacturer behind the Terminus railgun — produced the Entropy Pistol for a purpose that even veteran intelligence operators find disturbing: a weapon designed to kill slowly, painfully, and with no possibility of treatment. Acute radiation syndrome from EP-1 exposure follows a characteristic progression — nausea, then apparent recovery, then catastrophic organ failure as the irradiated tissue dies.

The weapon is the size of a large handgun and looks like nothing more than a matte-black tube with a trigger. There are no controls, no sights, and no indicators. The weapon either fires or it doesn't, and the target either dies in three days or survives with cancer they don't know about yet.

Grave Protocol Arms Terminus GPA-1 'Last Rites'#

A single-shot break-action railgun designed for absolute maximum velocity from the shortest possible barrel. The Terminus fires a 2mm tungsten needle at Mach 12 from a 40cm barrel, achieving penetration values that exceed rifles twice its length. The weapon is designed for a single engagement philosophy — one shot, one kill, then disappear.

Grave Protocol Arms is a manufacturer that exists only as a series of encrypted procurement channels. No facility has been identified, no employees named, and no corporate registration filed in any jurisdiction. The Terminus appears on the black market at irregular intervals, always in sealed cases with no documentation beyond a serial number etched into the receiver.

Forensic analysis of recovered Terminus weapons reveals manufacturing precision that exceeds any known commercial or military standard. Whoever builds these weapons has access to equipment that is not supposed to exist outside of Tier 5 fabrication facilities.

Gravimetric Collapse Charge GCC-9#

The GCC-9 represents OUROBOROS ENERGY's most aggressive weaponization of their gravimetric induction research — a technology platform the company officially licenses only for industrial compression and materials processing. The device generates an extremely short-duration gravimetric field spike, collapsing a roughly spherical volume of approximately 2 meters in diameter to a transient gravitational pressure roughly 400 times standard. The collapse event lasts approximately 40 milliseconds before field coherence fails and the compressed material is explosively rebounded outward. The inward collapse and outward rebound together constitute the weapon's kill mechanism.

The inward phase crushes everything within the primary radius — biological tissue, structural components, armor plating — into a dense, briefly coherent mass. The rebound phase then expels this compressed material at velocities sufficient to cause catastrophic fragmentation damage out to 15 meters. The resulting debris field is unusual: instead of conventional shrapnel, the rebound produces hyperdense compressed fragments of whatever was caught in the primary collapse, including bone, metal, and polymer fused together under the brief high-gravity event. Forensic investigators describe GCC-9 wound profiles as 'impossible' — fragmentation wounds containing materials from multiple sources compressed into single projectiles.

OUROBOROS ENERGY has invested significant legal resources in suppressing public knowledge of the GCC-9, arguing that the device is a classified industrial tool and that its appearance on the black market represents theft rather than distribution. Field operators who have used the weapon describe a profound psychological effect — the brief visual distortion of the collapse event, a moment where light bends visibly around the detonation point, has led to the name 'The Folding.' There are unverified reports that targets caught at the edge of the primary radius survive with gravitational trauma to dense-tissue organs that manifests days after exposure.

Gravimetric Induction Pistol GIP-4 'Undertow'#

The Gravimetric Induction Pistol operates on a principle that remains proprietary to OUROBOROS ENERGY despite years of competitor reverse-engineering attempts: it generates a localized gravimetric anomaly at range by briefly inducing a controlled mass-energy fluctuation through a compact induction array derived from OUROBOROS's experimental power generation research. In practical terms, the weapon projects a field approximately 40 centimeters in diameter that, for a duration of 0.6 to 2.4 seconds, increases effective gravitational acceleration within that field to between 4G and 9G depending on charge level. Targets caught in the field experience sudden, extreme downward force — enough to collapse joints, fracture load-bearing bones, and rupture intervertebral discs at high settings. At low settings, it is sufficient to pin a standing target to the floor and prevent movement.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the induction array for entirely different purposes — specifically, for manipulating heavy industrial components in confined spaces where mechanical lifting equipment cannot operate. The weaponization of the technology was, by most accounts, accidental: an industrial incident in which a malfunctioning array pinned three workers to a catwalk for several minutes before losing power demonstrated the technology's potential in a way that OUROBOROS's defense applications division found difficult to ignore. The GIP-4 is the fourth iteration of the resulting weapon program, and the first to achieve a form factor small enough to be carried as a sidearm.

The Undertow has acquired a reputation for the specific, recognizable nature of the injuries it produces. Physicians who treat gravitational compression injuries can identify them immediately — the pattern of skeletal damage, the characteristic joint failures, the bruising geometry — and this has become a forensic liability for operators. In GLMZ, 'gravity bruising' is increasingly recognized by both law enforcement and insurance forensics, making the Undertow less useful for operators who require deniability. Those who don't require deniability, however, find it extraordinarily effective.

Gravitic Shear Pistol GSP-7 'Tidal'#

The GSP-7 generates a localized tidal gradient — a microscale differential in gravitational field strength across a 15–20 centimeter target zone — using a pair of counter-rotating superconducting mass rings embedded in the weapon's cylindrical body. The gradient is projected as a focused columnar field approximately 3 centimeters in diameter at the point of emission, expanding to roughly 18 centimeters at optimal range. Within this column, the difference in gravitational pull between the near and far edges of the field is sufficient to impose significant shear stress on materials and tissue, stretching and tearing structures along the field axis without any projectile or beam making contact.

The practical effect on unprotected biological targets at full output is severe internal trauma along the field axis — tearing of connective tissue, rupture of fluid-filled structures, and in sustained exposure, fracture of cortical bone. The weapon does not burn, does not leave entry wounds, and produces no visible beam. Forensic examiners encountering GSP-7 casualties without prior knowledge of the weapon frequently misattribute the damage to blunt force or crush injury from environmental sources. This forensic ambiguity is the GSP-7's most valued characteristic in certain professional circles.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the GSP-7 under a research and development program nominally aimed at materials testing — specifically, evaluating shear resistance in structural composites under variable gravitational loading. The weapons application was, by most accounts within TESSERA, an open secret from the second prototype. Current production is limited, the supply chain is deliberately obscure, and TESSERA officially categorizes the GSP-7 as a 'field gradient analysis instrument' in all public documentation.

Graviton Compression Emitter GCE-3 'Flatline'#

The GCE-3 generates a focused graviton field projection that temporarily increases the effective gravitational force acting on a target volume by a factor of between 8 and 22 times standard gravity, depending on output setting. The effect is not a beam in the electromagnetic sense — it is a localized distortion of spacetime curvature within a defined area approximately 1.5 meters in diameter at standard operating range. Targets within the field experience sudden, catastrophic increases in effective body weight: at 8G, an unaugmented human experiences immediate skeletal stress fractures and cardiovascular collapse; at 22G, soft tissue rupture is near-instantaneous. The weapon was developed by Ouroboros Energy as a theoretical physics demonstration platform before its military applications became apparent and Arcturus Defense Solutions acquired exclusive licensing rights.

The GCE-3's technological foundation draws on the same graviton manipulation research that underlies GLMZ's commercial anti-gravity transit infrastructure, miniaturized and weaponized in a form that remains deeply controversial among the scientific community. The emitter core contains a crystalline graviton lens array that focuses the field projection with high spatial precision — the 1.5-meter effect radius means trained operators can affect a single target in a crowd without impacting bystanders, though field edge effects at the periphery of the compression zone cause significant discomfort and disorientation in adjacent individuals. The weapon's power requirements are enormous by handheld standards, necessitating a dedicated backpack power unit connected by a reinforced umbilical.

The GCE-3 is one of the most legally contentious weapons in GLMZ. Its use at a labor suppression event in the Palladian Construction sector in 2197 — where seventeen workers were killed and the incident was initially classified as a 'structural collapse' — remains an open wound in the city's political landscape. Ouroboros Energy has faced ongoing regulatory pressure over its foundational research, and the weapon's existence is technically classified at the municipal government level, though this classification is widely understood to be a legal fiction.

Guardian Compact Telescoping Rod CTR-1 'Extend'#

The Guardian CTR-1 is a telescoping shock rod designed explicitly around the problem of concealability. Collapsed, it measures just 22 centimeters — short enough to sit in a jacket pocket, a large purse, or a vehicle door compartment without obvious profile. A sharp outward flick of the wrist deploys the three-section aluminum-alloy shaft to its full 52-centimeter operational length, locking each section with an audible click. The contact electrode at the tip activates automatically on full extension if the safety thumb switch is pre-engaged, a design choice that has generated some controversy around accidental discharge during deployment.

Guardian positions the CTR-1 firmly in the consumer self-defense market, advertising it with imagery of night-shift workers, rideshare drivers, and healthcare staff navigating Tier 2 transit corridors after dark. It delivers 40,000 volts at a fixed output, slightly lower than dedicated security batons, but sufficient to startle and deter most threats. The internal battery is non-removable and charges via USB-Ω, the universal charging standard of 2180, giving it the same charging convenience as a personal device. Battery life is rated at approximately 25 discharges.

The CTR-1's deployment mechanism has been involved in several documented personal injury cases — primarily users accidentally shocking themselves or bystanders during the extension motion. Guardian has issued two firmware updates to the safety interlock system and settled the resulting litigation quietly. The product remains on shelves and continues to sell extremely well.

  • A CTR-1 recovered at a crime scene shows signs of modification — the auto-activate interlock has been bypassed and the discharge circuit rewired to fire repeatedly on a timer. Someone built a trap weapon, and the victim it was used on isn't talking.

Guardian CS-7 SecureSpray#

The Guardian CS-7 SecureSpray is a mid-tier dual-agent aerosol combining a 2% CS (2-chlorobenzalmalononitrile) lachrymatory compound with a 0.5% OC amplifier, suspended in a hydrofluorocarbon propellant rated for stable discharge across a temperature range of -10°C to 45°C. It is the standard-issue crowd and personal control spray for contracted security firms, private building management companies, and licensed corporate security auxiliaries operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 zones. The canister is significantly larger than consumer-grade options — approximately 180ml — with an ergonomic overmold grip, a rotating nozzle head offering cone or stream patterns, and a tamper-evident seal ring for accountability tracking.

The CS component produces a rapid and pronounced tearing and burning response in mucosal tissue, with secondary effects including coughing, chest tightness, and disorientation. The OC amplifier extends the inflammatory response and increases effectiveness against partially augmented targets whose respiratory systems remain biological. Guardian markets the CS-7 as a 'compliance facilitation tool' in its B2B literature, and most purchasers are institutional — building security firms, transit authority contractors, and mid-tier corporate campus guards. Individual licensing is available but carries a background verification requirement.

The CS-7 has a reasonably strong reputation for reliability and consistent performance, though critics within the civil liberties advocacy space have raised concerns about its deployment in enclosed residential environments, where the CS agent can persist for several hours and affect uninvolved residents through shared ventilation systems.

Guardian PocketShock PSR-1 'Nudge'#

The Guardian PSR-1 is a micro stun rod approximately the size and weight of a thick marker pen — 14 centimeters long, 1.8 centimeters in diameter, weighing 45 grams. One end is a pocket clip and recessed charge indicator; the other is a blunt contact tip with a single annular electrode. Inside is a single-use compressed capacitor assembly that stores enough energy for three full discharges at 35,000 volts before the capacitor is depleted, at which point the unit is discarded. There is no recharge port — the PSR-1 is a disposable product, sold in two-packs and four-packs at Tier 2 convenience outlets, pharmacies, and transit hub vending machines.

Guardian designed the PSR-1 around the concept of last-resort personal defense — a device so small and so simple that it offers a meaningful option to people who would carry nothing else. The activation mechanism is a deliberate squeeze-and-twist: the user grips the device firmly and rotates the upper third 90 degrees, which both arms the discharge and moves the contact tip to the active position. This prevents pocket activation while remaining operable under stress with one hand. The three-discharge limit is not a compromise — Guardian's research indicated that most defensive incidents requiring a shock weapon require one to two discharges, and a three-discharge limit keeps the capacitor assembly small enough for the form factor.

The PSR-1 is the most widely sold shock device in GLMZ by unit volume. Its Φ28 two-pack price point makes it accessible to Tier 1 residents in a way that no licensed security product is. Guardian's marketing for the PSR-1 is deliberately quiet — no dramatic imagery, no explicit weapon framing, just the phrase 'small enough to forget you have it, until you need it.'

In Tier 1 communities, the four-pack is a common gift between friends, family members, or neighbors — a quiet acknowledgment of shared vulnerability that doesn't require conversation.

Guardian Systems DermAlert DA-2 'Scarlet'#

The DermAlert DA-2 is Guardian Systems' dedicated dermal irritant spray, developed as a complement to their broader personal and institutional security product line. The active compound, GS-Urticant-2, is a synthetic urticant — a contact irritant that triggers mast cell degranulation and histamine cascade in exposed skin tissue, producing immediate intense inflammation, hive-like wheals, and a burning, crawling sensation that subjects consistently describe as unbearable within thirty seconds of exposure. Critically, GS-Urticant-2 is not a pain-channel agonist in the conventional sense — it does not activate TRPV1 channels and thus provides no cross-resistance with OC-tolerant individuals or those with pain-dampening chrome. The inflammatory response is immunological rather than neurological, bypassing most standard pain-tolerance augmentation.

The DA-2 is packaged in a distinctive red-and-black canister with a wide-fan nozzle optimized for sweeping deployment across crowds or through doorways. The compound produces a visible reddish aerosol mist — the product's 'Scarlet' designation — which serves a secondary purpose as a visual deterrent and crowd-movement indicator. GS-Urticant-2 settles on clothing and remains active for approximately two hours, meaning subjects cannot simply move away from the initial deployment area and expect relief — the compound travels with them.

Guardian markets the DA-2 heavily to Tier 2 and 3 venue security, transit security, and residential building security services as a step up from basic OC spray without the licensing burden of more restricted compounds. The product's effectiveness against augmented individuals has made it popular in environments where the security staff cannot reliably assess the augmentation status of potential threats.

HarborTech SafeScream SS-1 'Banshee'#

A keychain-sized personal alarm that emits a 142-decibel omnidirectional sonic burst when activated, producing a sound loud enough to cause immediate pain and disorientation at close range while alerting anyone within a 200-meter radius. The SS-1 activates via a pull-pin mechanism — yank the pin and the device screams until the pin is reinserted or the battery depletes, whichever comes first. The frequency is specifically calibrated to the human pain threshold: a warbling tone between 2,800 and 3,400 Hz that is physically impossible to ignore.

HarborTech designed the SS-1 after analyzing thousands of assault reports and finding that the single most effective deterrent was not pain or incapacitation but attention. Muggers, assailants, and opportunistic criminals in GLMZ rely on isolation and anonymity — the SS-1 eliminates both by making the attack the loudest thing happening within two city blocks.

The device costs Φ12 and runs on a standard coin cell battery that provides six minutes of continuous output. HarborTech distributes them through convenience stores, transit station kiosks, and community safety programs. In some Tier 1 neighborhoods, they are given away free by mutual aid organizations. The SS-1 is probably the single most widely carried self-defense device in GLMZ, surpassing even the SentryGuard PS-1 in sheer numbers.

The sound has become so associated with danger that HarborTech had to issue guidance asking people not to use it for non-emergency purposes after a series of 'Banshee pranks' caused neighborhood-wide panic responses.

Hearthstone Firearms Defender SMG HDS-5 'Hearth Guard'#

The HDS-5 Hearth Guard is a semi-automatic-only carbine chambered in 9mm brass-cased, designed for civilian home and business defense. Hearthstone Firearms deliberately restricted the weapon to semi-automatic operation to avoid regulatory classification as a military weapon, keeping it legal in jurisdictions where automatic weapons are prohibited. The result is a 9mm carbine with a 16-round magazine, basic iron sights, and no electronic components.

The Hearth Guard's design emphasizes safety for untrained users. The manual safety is oversized and color-coded — red for fire, white for safe. The magazine release requires deliberate two-finger operation to prevent accidental drops. The trigger pull is a heavy 4.5 kilograms to prevent negligent discharge. Every design decision prioritizes preventing accidents over maximizing combat effectiveness.

At Φ350, the Hearth Guard is the cheapest long gun Hearthstone produces. It sells in enormous volumes to small business owners, residential cooperatives, and individuals who need a weapon more capable than a handgun but cannot afford or legally possess a military-grade platform. The weapon is basic, safe, and reliable — exactly what its customers need.

Hearthstone Firearms Defender-38 'Snubnose'#

The Hearthstone Defender-38 is a five-shot double-action revolver chambered in .38 Special with a two-inch barrel, designed as the ultimate simple defensive weapon. The frame is aluminum alloy to reduce weight, the hammer is shrouded to prevent snagging on clothing during draw, and there is no adjustable sight — just a milled groove in the top strap that serves as a rudimentary sight channel.

The Snubnose is the revolver equivalent of the Guardian-12 — a weapon for people who want something simple, safe, and effective at arm's length. The two-inch barrel makes it genuinely pocketable, and the shrouded hammer allows a smooth draw from a coat pocket without catching on fabric. Five rounds of .38 Special won't win a prolonged firefight, but at the ranges where this weapon will be used — typically less than three meters — the point is to survive the first ten seconds.

Hearthstone sells the Defender-38 with a soft fabric pocket holster and a five-round speedloader. Their marketing is characteristically practical: 'Five answers to one question.' The weapon sells steadily across all tiers, from Shelf grandmothers who keep one in their housecoat pocket to Mid executives who slip one into their overcoat as a deep-concealment backup.

Hearthstone Firearms Guardian-12 'Bedside'#

The Hearthstone Guardian-12 is a double-action semi-automatic pistol chambered in .380 ACP, designed and marketed specifically for home defense in Shelf and lower-Mid residential blocks. The frame is oversized for the caliber, making it easy to grip with shaking or untrained hands. The trigger pull in double-action mode is deliberately heavy at 5.5kg to prevent negligent discharge.

The Guardian-12 ships with a built-in trigger lock, a loaded chamber indicator visible in darkness through a tritium-painted port, and an instruction manual written at a fourth-grade reading level in fourteen languages. Hearthstone designed every aspect of this weapon for people who have never held a gun before and hope they never have to fire one. The heavy trigger, the visible chamber indicator, the oversized grip — all of it prioritizes safety over performance.

The Bedside is the best-selling firearm in Shelf residential districts. Families keep them in nightstand drawers and kitchen cabinets, loaded with hollow-point rounds that Hearthstone bundles in the box. It is not a weapon for professionals. It is a weapon for parents who heard gunshots last night and decided they needed something between themselves and the door.

Hearthstone Firearms HF-30 'Homestead'#

Hearthstone Firearms caters to the civilian defense market with weapons that are deliberately simple, deliberately rugged, and deliberately affordable. The HF-30 Homestead is a semi-automatic rifle chambered in 5.56mm with a traditional layout, wooden furniture options, and no electronic components whatsoever. No BCI link. No smart-link. No onboard computer. Just a rifle.

The Homestead uses a conventional brass-cased cartridge rather than the caseless ammunition that dominates the military market. This is a deliberate choice — brass-cased 5.56mm is manufactured by dozens of small operations across GLMZ and remains available when caseless supply chains collapse. The rifle's manual of arms requires no technical training beyond basic firearms operation, making it accessible to communities without military experience.

At Φ600, the Homestead is the cheapest new-production rifle on the market. Hearthstone sells them in bulk to settlement cooperatives and community defense funds. The weapon won't impress anyone who has handled a Mandate or a Consensus, but it puts an accurate, reliable rifle in the hands of people who need one and can't afford anything else.

Hearthstone Firearms Homestead-12 'Door Slam'#

The Hearthstone Homestead-12 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a five-round tubular magazine and an 18-inch barrel. It is the cheapest functional shotgun in GLMZ, manufactured with the same cost-conscious approach that defines Hearthstone's product line — stamped steel receiver, hardwood stock finished with lacquer rather than oil, and a bead front sight that serves as the only aiming reference.

The Door Slam is the Shelf home defense standard. Where the Guardian-12 pistol provides comfort, the Homestead provides capability — a 12-gauge shotgun loaded with buckshot is effective against nearly any unarmored threat at room distance, regardless of the shooter's training level. The pump action is simple to operate, visually intimidating when racked, and mechanically reliable in a way that budget semi-automatics cannot match.

Hearthstone sells the Homestead-12 with a box of twenty-five buckshot shells and a trigger lock. Their marketing acknowledges the weapon's real purpose without euphemism: 'When they come through the door, be on the other side of this.' The weapon sells by the tens of thousands annually and constitutes the backbone of Shelf residential defense.

Hearthstone Firearms Hunter's Precision HHP-7 'Longreach'#

The HHP-7 Longreach is a bolt-action precision rifle designed for frontier hunters and settlement defenders who need accuracy at distance without electronic assistance. The weapon chambers .308 brass-cased — a legacy cartridge that Hearthstone perpetuates because it is manufactured by dozens of small ammunition producers across GLMZ. The bolt-action operation is slower than semi-automatic alternatives but provides a rigid lockup that maximizes accuracy.

The Longreach comes with a fixed 10x optical scope of surprisingly good quality, manufactured in-house by Hearthstone's optics division. The scope features a ballistic-drop compensating reticle calibrated specifically for the .308 at standard atmospheric conditions, allowing holdover adjustments without turret dialing. The rifle's walnut stock is hand-checkered — an anachronistic touch that Hearthstone maintains because their customers value craftsmanship.

At Φ1,200, the Longreach provides genuine precision capability at a price that frontier communities can afford. Its bolt action and legacy cartridge are limitations by military standards, but for a settlement defender engaging threats at 500-700 meters, the rifle delivers. The HHP-7 has put more game on more tables and deterred more threats at more settlement gates than any smart-scoped wonder weapon ever manufactured.

Hearthstone Firearms Model 9 'Payday'#

The Hearthstone Model 9 is a bottom-of-the-barrel semi-automatic pistol chambered in 9x19mm, manufactured from injection-molded polymer and stamped steel components. The barrel is unrifled on early production runs — a cost-cutting measure that Hearthstone has never officially acknowledged. The trigger pull is heavy and gritty, the sights are rudimentary plastic posts, and the magazine release has a documented tendency to drop magazines under recoil.

The Payday is the firearm of last resort for people who cannot afford anything better. It is sold in blister packs at convenience stores in Shelf districts, often alongside prepaid comm cards and synthetic protein bars. Shelf security forces confiscate thousands annually, but the economics of the weapon make replacement trivial — a new Model 9 costs less than a decent meal in the Mids.

Despite its reputation as disposable junk, the Payday has an outsized cultural presence. It appears in countless Shelf folk songs and street poetry as a symbol of desperation and defiance. The phrase 'pulling a Payday' has entered common slang meaning to attempt something with inadequate tools and pure nerve.

Hearthstone Firearms Plinker-22 'Tin Can'#

The Hearthstone Plinker-22 is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in .22 LR, built with a zinc-alloy slide and polymer frame that together weigh less than a loaded magazine for most duty pistols. The weapon is sold in the sporting goods section of general retailers alongside fishing rods and camp stoves. It costs less than a quality pair of boots.

The Plinker serves two populations with zero overlap. Recreational shooters in the Mids buy it for target practice and weekend plinking at sanctioned ranges — it is cheap to shoot, fun to use, and mechanically simple enough to teach firearms basics. Shelf residents buy it because it is the second-cheapest gun available and marginally more reliable than the cheapest. In either context, nobody mistakes it for a serious defensive weapon.

Hearthstone makes no pretense about the Plinker's capabilities. Their marketing materials describe it as 'recreational' and 'introductory,' and the packaging includes a prominent disclaimer that the weapon is 'not recommended as a primary personal defense tool.' This disclaimer satisfies Hearthstone's legal department while tacitly acknowledging that many buyers will ignore it entirely.

Hearthstone Firearms Ranch SMG HRS-3 'Cattleman'#

The HRS-3 Cattleman is Hearthstone's only automatic weapon — a simple, robust 9mm submachine gun designed for agricultural defense against wildlife threats and livestock predators. The weapon features a semi-auto/three-round burst selector with no full-auto option, keeping the rate of fire controlled for untrained ranch operators. The 20-round magazine provides sufficient capacity for most encounters without the bulk of military magazines.

True to Hearthstone's philosophy, the Cattleman has no electronic components. Iron sights, manual safety, mechanical trigger. The weapon is finished in a corrosion-resistant matte ceramic coating designed for years of outdoor storage in ranch buildings and vehicle gun racks. The action is intentionally over-gassed to cycle reliably with dirty, corroded, or low-quality ammunition — the kind of ammunition available at frontier trading posts.

At Φ500, the Cattleman fills the gap between Hearthstone's semi-auto Hearth Guard and the security-oriented weapons of larger manufacturers. It provides controlled automatic firepower to communities that face threats from modified wildlife, feral synthetics, and the occasional human predator. The burst limiter prevents untrained users from dumping ammunition in panic, imposing discipline that their training does not.

Hearthstone Firearms Scout Rifle HSR-10 'Wanderer'#

The HSR-10 Wanderer is a lightweight semi-automatic rifle designed for frontier scouts, surveyors, and travelers who need a weapon that handles both two-legged and four-legged threats without weighing them down. Chambered in 6.5mm brass-cased, the Wanderer offers better range and terminal performance than the company's 5.56mm Homestead while maintaining Hearthstone's signature no-electronics design philosophy.

The rifle weighs just 2.9 kilograms thanks to a skeletonized aluminum receiver and carbon-fiber-wrapped barrel. A fixed 4x optical scope provides magnification for medium-range engagements, and the smooth two-stage trigger delivers consistent pulls that reward patient marksmanship. The 15-round magazine keeps the profile slim for carry, and the weapon's overall length with folding stock collapsed fits comfortably in a backpack frame.

Hearthstone developed the Wanderer after surveying frontier operators who reported that existing rifles were either too heavy for extended foot travel, too dependent on electronics that failed in remote areas, or too expensive to risk in wilderness conditions. The HSR-10 answers all three complaints with a rifle that is light, analog, and priced at Φ900.

Hearthstone Firearms Sentinel-9 'Block Watch'#

The Hearthstone Sentinel-9 is a full-size semi-automatic pistol chambered in 9x19mm, representing Hearthstone's attempt to move upmarket from their Shelf-focused product line. The frame is reinforced polymer with steel slide rails, the barrel is conventionally rifled rather than the cast barrels found in their budget offerings, and the trigger is a clean striker-fired mechanism with an acceptable pull weight.

The Sentinel-9 costs roughly three times what a Payday costs and delivers roughly ten times the performance. For Shelf residents who have saved enough to upgrade from disposable firearms, it represents the entry point into 'real' gun ownership — a weapon that can be maintained, accessorized, and relied upon over years of use rather than months. Hearthstone designed it as a bridge product: familiar enough to their existing customer base to feel accessible, competent enough to earn respect outside Shelf districts.

The Block Watch nickname emerged from community defense groups in upper-Shelf neighborhoods who pooled resources to equip their members with Sentinel-9s instead of the usual assortment of Paydays and Tin Cans. The improvement in reliability and accuracy was immediate and measurable, and the Sentinel-9 became a symbol of Shelf communities investing in their own protection.

Hearthstone Firearms Single-20 'Farmhand'#

The Hearthstone Single-20 is a single-shot break-action shotgun chambered in 20 gauge with a 26-inch barrel and an exposed hammer. The weapon holds one round, fires it, breaks open to eject the spent shell, and accepts a new round. It is the absolute minimum viable shotgun — simpler even than the Stagecoach, with one barrel instead of two and a correspondingly lower price.

The Farmhand is the first gun many Shelf families own. Its single-shot capacity is a limitation that Hearthstone reframes as a safety feature — you cannot fire more rounds than you intend to, and the break-action gives a clear visual indication of whether the weapon is loaded. For families with children, the simplicity and visual safety of the Farmhand provide comfort that more capable but more complex weapons cannot.

The 20-gauge chambering reduces recoil to a level manageable by smaller-framed adults and older teenagers, making the Farmhand the de facto training shotgun for families who can't afford separate training and defensive weapons. Children learn to shoot on it, parents keep it loaded by the door at night, and when it finally wears out, they buy another one for less than the cost of a week's protein rations.

Hearthstone Firearms Trail-357 'Pathfinder'#

The Hearthstone Trail-357 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum with a five-inch barrel and a stainless steel frame finished in a brushed satin that resists the elements. Hearthstone designed the Pathfinder for residents of the peripheral territories and rural settlements who need a reliable sidearm for outdoor carry in harsh conditions — dust, moisture, temperature extremes, and the unpredictable threats of the wastelands.

The Pathfinder is Hearthstone's best weapon by a wide margin. Where their Shelf-focused products prioritize minimum cost, the Trail-357 prioritizes ruggedness. The frame is overbuilt for the caliber, the cylinder lock-up is tight, and the internal parts are treated with a corrosion-resistant coating that keeps the action smooth even after weeks of exposure to gritty environments. The five-inch barrel extracts full velocity from .357 Magnum ammunition while keeping the weapon holsterable.

In the peripheral territories, the Pathfinder has become something of a standard. Settlement defense groups carry them, expedition teams pack them as backup, and the few individuals who still work the land between GLMZ's developed zones rely on them as multi-purpose tools — personal defense, pest control, and signal device. The weapon is also compatible with .38 Special for cheaper everyday carry.

Hearthstone Firearms Watchtower Rifle HWR-4 'Vigil'#

The HWR-4 Vigil is a semi-automatic DMR designed for settlement watchtower duty — the specific role of a defender stationed in an elevated position providing overwatch for a community's perimeter. The weapon chambers 6.5mm brass-cased through a 550mm barrel with a fixed 8x scope, delivering 1.5-MOA accuracy at 700 meters. Like all Hearthstone weapons, the Vigil contains no electronic components.

The weapon's design reflects its intended deployment. The stock has an integral cheek rest optimized for downward-angle shooting from elevated positions. The barrel is free-floated within a ventilated handguard designed for sustained observation in hot climates. The scope mount is reinforced against the impact of the weapon being set down repeatedly on stone or concrete watchtower ledges. Every detail serves the reality of long hours in a tower, watching, waiting, and occasionally shooting.

At Φ1,800, the Vigil is priced for settlement procurement — communities buying weapons for their watch rotation rather than individual operators. Hearthstone sells them in watchtower kits that include the rifle, scope, cleaning supplies, and a weather-resistant storage case designed to hang from a tower wall. The complete kit runs Φ2,100, and many settlements maintain multiple kits at their watchtower positions.

Hearthstone Firearms Youth-20 'First Step'#

The Hearthstone Youth-20 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 20 gauge with a shortened 13-inch length of pull, a 22-inch barrel, and a four-round tubular magazine. The weapon is scaled down from full-size proportions to fit younger or smaller-framed shooters, with a reduced-weight trigger spring and a shortened pump stroke that requires less force to cycle.

The First Step is Hearthstone's answer to a grim reality: in the Shelf and peripheral territories, young people may need to use a firearm for defense, and a weapon that doesn't fit them is worse than no weapon at all. The Youth-20 is sized for adolescents and small adults, with ergonomics that allow proper technique development rather than the compensating grip and stance that full-size weapons force on undersized shooters.

Hearthstone's marketing for the Youth-20 is carefully balanced between practical and aspirational. They avoid depicting children with weapons but clearly communicate that the product exists for young people. The packaging includes a comprehensive safety manual, a trigger lock, and a letter to parents that reads like a careful legal document wrapped around genuine concern. The weapon is available only through licensed dealers who are required to verify that the purchaser is a legal guardian.

Helical Vortex Penetrator HVP-4 'Corkscrew'#

The HVP-4 fires a magnetically stabilized tungsten-ceramic projectile wrapped in a rotating electromagnetic sheath that induces a tight helical spin at velocities exceeding 4,200 meters per second. Unlike conventional rifling, the spin is not imparted by barrel grooves but by a series of phased electromagnetic coils along the accelerator rail that fire in precise sequence, allowing the rotation rate to be tuned dynamically via a thumb-wheel adjuster on the receiver. At maximum spin, the projectile generates a secondary vacuum vortex behind its path capable of destabilizing soft tissue and lightweight armor panels through torsional shear stress alone.

What distinguishes the Corkscrew from conventional railguns is its Torsional Cavity Induction system — a secondary coil near the muzzle imparts a brief counter-rotating field to the projectile's outer ceramic sleeve just before exit. This causes the sleeve to fracture in a controlled spiral pattern mid-flight, releasing the denser tungsten penetrator core with an enhanced rotational wobble that defeats layered composite armor by exploiting the angular gaps between laminate sheets. The result is a weapon that transitions from a clean penetrator at close range to a tumbling, spiraling wound-maker at extended distances.

The HVP-4 is a long, ungainly rifle with a pronounced coil housing that runs the length of the barrel, giving it a corrugated, industrial appearance. It runs hot — sustained fire without the integrated coolant sleeve risks coil burnout — but in the hands of a trained operator it is regarded as one of the most mechanically elegant anti-materiel solutions available outside of military procurement channels.

Hemolytic Vapor Induction Carbine#

The HVIC-3 operates by projecting a tuned aerosol of catalytic nanoparticles into the breathing zone of a target, where they are subsequently activated by a focused near-infrared trigger pulse from the carbine's secondary emitter. Once inhaled or absorbed transdermally, the particles bind to hemoglobin iron sites and initiate a controlled oxidative cascade, forcing red blood cells into a premature lysis cycle. The effect begins within ninety seconds of exposure and manifests as rapidly progressing hypoxia, subcutaneous hemorrhaging, and systemic pressure collapse. Range is limited to approximately eighteen meters in open air, though enclosed spaces dramatically amplify dispersal efficiency.

What separates the HVIC-3 from cruder aerosol weapons is its selectivity system. Operators can pre-load a biometric exclusion profile — a genetic or proteomic signature — allowing the carbine to suppress activation in targeted individuals while the cloud remains lethal to everyone else in the zone. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets this as a 'precision population management tool,' which has done little to soften the weapon's reputation. The carbine itself resembles an oversized pump-action shotgun with a bulbous canister housing beneath the barrel, and emits a faint copper smell during discharge that veteran operators have learned to treat as a serious warning sign.

The nickname 'Redmist' comes not from the aerosol itself, which is invisible, but from the subcutaneous hemorrhaging that gives affected skin a mottled crimson flush in the final stages of exposure. 'The Blush' is used more sardonically, typically by the corporate security contractors who deploy it for crowd suppression in sealed transit hubs and processing centers.

Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector#

The Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector uses a focused beam of modulated microwave and near-infrared radiation tuned to the absorption and catalytic disruption frequencies of glycogen phosphorylase — the enzyme responsible for mobilizing stored glucose from the liver. By overwhelming hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity through thermal and photonic excitation, the weapon forces the complete and near-instantaneous liberation of all hepatic glycogen stores into the bloodstream, followed by rapid enzymatic exhaustion that prevents resynthesis. The result is a catastrophic glucose spike lasting approximately ninety seconds, followed by profound hypoglycemia as reserves are depleted and resynthesis is blocked. The target collapses into a hypoglycemic crisis within four to seven minutes.

The HGDP-2 is a weapon of delayed effect, which gives it a distinct tactical character. An operator can tag a target and withdraw entirely before the effect manifests. The initial exposure causes no pain, no visible wound, and no immediate behavioral change — the target simply walks away feeling briefly warm. Minutes later, sweating, confusion, and motor failure set in, followed by loss of consciousness. Without immediate glucose intervention, the hypoglycemic crisis can progress to seizure and death within fifteen to twenty minutes. With intervention, the target survives but requires hours of medical support.

The projector's form factor resembles a standard industrial thermal scanner, providing effective cover in maintenance and technical environments. Ringo Corponation licenses the underlying photonic enzyme excitation technology for legitimate food processing applications, a fact that has been exploited extensively to launder the weapon's supply chain. The HGDP-2 is particularly dangerous to targets with diabetic or metabolic augmentations that suppress normal glucose regulatory responses, as these individuals have reduced capacity to self-correct even partial depletion.

Hepatic Vapor Pressure Burst Charge#

The Hepatic Vapor Pressure Burst Charge is a contact explosive designed for placement on surfaces where targets are expected to rest, lean, or brace — vehicle seats, chair backs, wall panels, floor tiles. Its detonation sequence uses a ferroelectric compression initiator to generate a precisely shaped pressure wave tuned to maximize coupling with hepatic parenchymal tissue. The charge delivers its energy selectively to the liver's vascular architecture, triggering rapid vapor pressure buildup within sinusoidal spaces and causing catastrophic hepatic rupture with minimal blast damage to surrounding tissue or material.

The engineering basis for the HVPBC-2 emerged from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' agricultural research into livestock processing optimization — specifically, non-destructive pressure techniques for organ evaluation. The weaponized application was developed under a separate classified contract, though the technical lineage is visible to anyone who examines the ferroelectric compression profile. The charge is approximately the size of a playing card and 4mm thick, making it concealable within standard furnishings with no detectable profile under most security sweeps.

Targets struck by the HVPBC-2 experience an immediate sensation described by survivors as 'a punch from inside' followed by progressive right upper quadrant pain and rapid hemodynamic collapse. Because the external blast signature is minimal — a sharp crack audible only within a few meters — the HVPBC-2 is the weapon of choice for assassinations where the cause of death must appear medical. Coroners unfamiliar with the charge's signature frequently log cause of death as spontaneous hepatic hemorrhage.

Hollow Point Precision Needle Storm NP-8 'Acupuncture'#

A magnetically-accelerated micro-flechette weapon that fires clouds of 0.5mm titanium needles at extreme velocity. Each trigger pull releases approximately 500 needles in a cloud roughly 2 meters in diameter at 30 meters range. Individual needles lack stopping power, but the cumulative effect of hundreds of micro-penetrations produces rapid blood loss and systemic shock.

Hollow Point Precision designed the Acupuncture to exploit a gap in defensive technology — most armor systems are optimized for a few large impacts, not hundreds of micro-penetrations. The NP-8's needle cloud finds every seam, gap, joint, and exposed surface in a target's protection, turning armor from a defense into a container for the bleeding.

The weapon is nearly silent — the electromagnetic acceleration produces a soft hum, and the needles are too small to generate audible flight noise. Targets hit by a needle cloud initially feel nothing. Seconds later, they notice blood from hundreds of pinprick wounds. Seconds after that, they lose consciousness from the cumulative blood loss.

Hollow Point Precision Requiem HP-4 'Dirge'#

A suppressed anti-personnel precision rifle that fires subsonic fragmenting rounds designed to produce maximum wound trauma while minimizing over-penetration risk. Hollow Point Precision is a small manufacturer founded by a former field medic who understood exactly how to make a bullet kill efficiently.

The HP-4 fires a 9.3mm polymer-jacketed round that expands to 22mm upon tissue contact, fragmenting into six pre-scored petals that travel along divergent wound channels. This makes the Requiem ideal for urban environments where over-penetration endangers civilians.

The weapon's integral suppressor reduces its acoustic signature to 72 decibels — loud enough to be heard in an enclosed space, but easily lost in the ambient noise of GLMZ's urban environment.

Homegrown Blister Wash 'Shelf Special'#

No manufacturer. No registration. No safety data sheet. The Shelf Special is a category of improvised chemical spray assembled from industrial cleaning solvents, agricultural concentrates, and chemical precursors available through Meridian Municipal Supply's open-market distribution channels or salvaged from the industrial waste streams that flow through the Shelf's sub-level infrastructure. Formulas vary by maker and availability — the most common variants combine concentrated industrial degreaser base with either agricultural-grade capsaicin extract, phenol derivative rinse concentrate, or in more dangerous iterations, trace oxidizing agents recovered from battery recycling operations. The result is delivered in repurposed pressurized containers: cleaning spray bottles, modified aerosol cans, or improvised pump chambers made from scavenged plumbing components.

The effects of a Shelf Special are unpredictable in the truest sense. A batch made with degreaser and agricultural capsaicin produces an extremely aggressive OC-like effect with significantly deeper tissue penetration than commercial sprays — the industrial solvent carrier strips protective oils and drives the active compound into the dermis rather than sitting on the surface. A batch incorporating phenol derivatives produces chemical burns with delayed onset — a subject may not realize the severity of exposure for several minutes. Batches that include oxidizing agents or improperly neutralized industrial acids have produced outcomes ranging from severe chemical burns to respiratory failure. Makers rarely know exactly what they have until it is used.

The Shelf Special is not a product. It is a symptom — of poverty, of the reality that Tier 1 residents cannot access licensed self-defense tools, and of the chemical abundance of an industrial city whose waste products are more accessible to its poorest residents than its consumer goods. Law enforcement treats possession as a serious offense. Street medics treat exposure as a major emergency.

Hydrostatic Nerve Cradle HNC-3 'Swaddling'#

The Hydrostatic Nerve Cradle operates by projecting a precisely tuned hydrostatic field envelope around a target's body — a near-invisible shell of pressurized aqueous microparticles suspended in a charged ionic matrix. Once the envelope seals, internal pressure differentials are manipulated in real time, selectively compressing nerve clusters and vascular pathways without breaking skin. The effect is described by survivors as being 'held very tightly by something that knows exactly where to squeeze.' Victims remain conscious, mobile in theory, but functionally paralyzed as the cradle prioritizes motor pathway suppression over pain centers.

What distinguishes the HNC-3 from cruder pressure weapons is its neural feedback architecture, which reads bioelectric fluctuations through the ionic envelope and dynamically adjusts the pressure map. The weapon does not simply crush — it listens, and corrects. Targets who struggle or spike cortisol experience a tightening feedback loop. Calm targets are held in stasis. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS designed it nominally as a non-lethal restraint platform for high-value capture operations, though field reports consistently note that operators who hold the lock for more than forty seconds begin causing irreversible vascular damage.

The HNC-3 is shoulder-mounted with a wrist-linked targeting interface, requiring the operator to maintain line-of-sight within eighteen meters. It has a distinctive low hum during active lock — operators call it 'the lullaby's older sibling,' a reference to the SDE-4 that HELIX publicly denies. The weapon's cultural notoriety stems from its association with corporate extraction teams: it is the preferred tool of those who need someone alive but not resistant.

Ironically, high-end private security for the ultra-wealthy also uses it, rebranded as 'non-lethal executive protection.' Its dual identity — oppressor's tool and luxury service — makes it a flashpoint in class-politics discourse.

Hydrostatic Pressure Lance HPL-1 'Deepwater'#

The HPL-1 generates a coherent column of hydrodynamic pressure using a resonant fluid compression chamber fed by an onboard micro-reservoir of dense hydraulic fluid. The weapon does not project fluid outward — instead, it generates a standing wave of hydrostatic pressure in the air column between the emitter and the target, exploiting the body's own fluid content as the transmission medium. When the wave reaches a water-dense target (biological tissue, hydraulic systems, fluid-cooled electronics), it couples with the target's internal fluid and induces explosive hydrostatic overpressure within enclosed spaces: sinuses, joint capsules, the chambers of the heart, fluid-cooled cybernetic housings.

Palladian Construction originally developed the HPL-1's core technology for non-explosive demolition of water-saturated geological formations — the same hydrostatic coupling effect that destroys joint capsules works equally well on saturated rock strata and underwater structural elements. The weaponized variant was engineered by a Palladian subsidiary that was subsequently dissolved, with the technology licensed to a series of shell companies before eventually reaching street manufacture. The weapon's industrial origins are visible in its form factor: it looks like a construction tool, heavy and utilitarian, with none of the ergonomic refinement of purpose-built weapons.

Against unaugmented biological targets, the HPL-1 produces a spectrum of effects depending on range and power: at distance, joint pain and disorientation from sinus overpressure; at medium range, ruptured eardrums and hemorrhaging from sinus cavities; at close range, cardiac arrhythmia from heart chamber pressure spikes and potential joint dislocation as capsular fluid flashes to expanded state. Against fluid-cooled cybernetic systems, the weapon is catastrophically effective — it can detonate cooling jackets and pressure housings without any visible external impact.

Inductive Thermal Lance#

The Inductive Thermal Lance is a heavy close-combat weapon produced by Palladian Construction, originally developed as a field tool for emergency structural cutting in collapsed building scenarios. The ITL-5 consists of a 90-centimeter reinforced handle assembly connected to a 40-centimeter ferrous core lance tip surrounded by a tight helical induction coil. When powered, the coil generates a rapidly alternating magnetic field that induces eddy currents directly within the ferrous tip, heating it to operational temperature — approximately 900 degrees Celsius — within four seconds, without any external flame or combustion. The tip glows a deep amber-orange at operating temperature and maintains heat continuously while powered.

The transition from construction tool to weapon was, by most accounts, inevitable given the ITL-5's field profile. Palladian Construction workers in contested infrastructure zones began carrying them as combination tools and deterrents, and the design's robustness — built to function in debris fields, flooded basements, and chemically contaminated environments — made it a natural fit for the kinds of chaotic close-quarters scenarios common in GLMZ's lower districts. Palladian has never officially marketed the ITL-5 as a weapon, but their industrial sales division has been notably uninterested in investigating end-user applications, and modified versions with sharpened tips and shortened handles have been documented in the hands of non-construction personnel for years.

The ITL-5's combat profile is defined by its ability to defeat armor through thermal transfer rather than kinetic force. Against standard ballistic plate, the lance tip burns through the outer layer within seconds of sustained contact, defeating the material's protective properties before mechanical penetration is attempted. Against biological targets, the cauterizing effect of the weapon simultaneously wounds and seals — a grim feature that operators in extended engagements have described as 'efficient,' as it reduces the user's risk of exposure to target blood.

Ionic Shear Projector ISP-2 'Splitvolt'#

The ISP-2 generates a narrow planar sheet of ionized plasma approximately 1.4 meters long and 2 centimeters wide, sustained at close range by a pair of electromagnetic field guides mounted at the weapon's emitter fork. The plasma sheet is not a beam in the conventional sense — it does not project across distance. Instead, it functions as an extended melee cutting surface, maintained at temperatures exceeding 8,000 Kelvin along its active edge. The weapon is, in practical terms, an energy blade: wielded in close quarters, it cuts through most materials that conventional blades cannot, including hardened ceramic plating and lower-grade ballistic weaves.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the ISP-2 as a response to the increasing prevalence of subdermal armor implants in high-value targets — human tissue reinforced with ceramic mesh or carbon-fiber laminate that defeats conventional blades entirely. The plasma edge interacts with these materials through a combination of thermal ablation and ionic disruption, effectively 'unzipping' the molecular bonds of the implant matrix rather than cutting through it mechanically. Against unaugmented targets, wounds are cauterized on contact, producing less blood evidence and complicating forensic analysis.

The ISP-2 is notoriously difficult to use effectively. The plasma sheet requires the operator to maintain field guide alignment within tight tolerances — any impact to the emitter fork risks field collapse, which releases a brief but violent ionic discharge that can injure the user. Training programs for the weapon are extensive and proprietary to Zheng-Dao's licensed operator network. On the street, self-taught users are identifiable by the characteristic burn scarring on their dominant forearm.

Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle ITR-5 'Ashmaker'#

The Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle functions by projecting a sustained stream of superheated ionized gas — technically a directed plasma jet — at ranges far exceeding conventional flamethrower technology. The key innovation is the magnetic confinement collar at the barrel's terminus, a toroidal field generator that compresses the plasma stream into a coherent column and prevents the lateral thermal bleed that makes conventional plasma projection impractical at range. The result is a weapon that delivers extreme thermal energy to a target at distances up to 60 meters with a column diameter of approximately 8 centimeters at point of impact.

Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION under a military infrastructure contract, the ITR-5 was originally intended for demolition work — specifically for cutting through reinforced structural elements in contested urban environments. Its adoption as a direct combat weapon was, by TESSERA's own internal communications, 'an unanticipated market development.' The weapon's effect on unarmored biological targets is severe and rapid: the plasma column causes flash vaporization of surface tissue and ignition of underlying structures within 2 seconds of sustained contact. Armored targets experience accelerated surface ablation and heat transfer sufficient to cause incapacitation through cookoff of interior equipment.

The Ashmaker has a complex cultural footprint. Its association with demolition work gives it a certain blue-collar credibility in the construction and infrastructure sectors, where modified civilian variants are not uncommon for cutting operations. Its use as a weapon is associated primarily with large-scale violence — building clearances, punitive actions by corporate security against squatter communities — and it carries a stigma that most individual operators find professionally undesirable. Carrying one signals either professional demolition work or a willingness to engage in atrocity.

Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'#

A squad support weapon manufactured by the Iron Meridian Cooperative, a worker-owned defense manufacturer that produces equipment for community defense organizations and municipal security forces. The Backbone is a conventional belt-fed 7.62mm machine gun built for reliability, repairability, and sustained fire with minimal maintenance.

The IMC-3 contains no smart electronics, no BCI integration, and no electromagnetic acceleration. It is a mechanically-operated weapon that uses conventional chemical propellant ammunition and a gas-piston action refined over decades. Every component is designed for field repair with hand tools, and the weapon's open-bolt design runs cool enough for sustained fire without barrel changes.

The Backbone represents a philosophical counterpoint to the high-technology weapons that dominate corporate arsenals. It does not guide rounds, project shields, or coordinate with networked systems. It simply fires bullets, reliably and continuously, for as long as the operator feeds it ammunition.

Kang-Petrov Arms KP-10C 'Bullpup'#

The Kang-Petrov KP-10C is a compact semi-automatic pistol chambered in 10mm Auto, designed as a scaled-down version of their duty platform for concealed carry. The barrel is trimmed to nine centimeters and the grip shortened to accept flush-fit eight-round magazines. The result is a punchy, snappy little weapon that puts 10mm power into a package small enough for inside-waistband carry.

The Bullpup is not comfortable to shoot. The abbreviated grip makes maintaining control during rapid fire challenging, and the 10mm recoil in the lightened frame is aggressive. Kang-Petrov includes an extended pinky rest magazine baseplate in the box — a tacit admission that most shooters cannot grip the weapon adequately with the flush magazine. But comfort was never the point. The KP-10C exists for people who want 10mm stopping power and refuse to carry a full-size pistol.

The weapon has found an unexpected niche among licensed couriers who transit between district tiers carrying high-value packages. The combination of concealability and stopping power suits their specific threat profile — they need a weapon that is invisible until required and decisive when deployed.

Kang-Petrov Arms KP-19 'Workhorse'#

The Kang-Petrov KP-19 is a full-size duty pistol chambered in 9x19mm, built on a steel-reinforced polymer frame with a cold-hammer-forged barrel. It represents the baseline of competent firearm engineering — nothing revolutionary, nothing deficient. The action is reliable, the trigger is acceptable, and the sights are adequate steel three-dot units that hold zero indefinitely.

The KP-19 is the standard-issue sidearm for dozens of private security companies, building security teams, and licensed personal protection operators throughout the Mids. Kang-Petrov's business model is volume and consistency — every KP-19 performs identically to every other KP-19, and replacement parts are available at any hardware vendor in GLMZ.

The Workhorse earned its nickname honestly. It is the pistol that guards carry when their employer doesn't care about brand prestige but does care about liability. It works, it keeps working, and when it finally wears out after tens of thousands of rounds, the replacement costs the same as a moderately expensive dinner.

Kang-Petrov Arms KP-22 Sport 'Plinkmaster'#

The Kang-Petrov KP-22 Sport is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in .22 LR, designed for recreational target shooting with the ergonomics and controls of the full-size KP duty platform. The weapon is mechanically identical in layout to the KP-19 — same safety position, same magazine release, same slide lock — allowing owners to practice fundamentals on cheap .22 ammunition before transitioning to their carry weapon.

The KP-22 Sport features an extended five-inch barrel with a bull profile for maximum accuracy, adjustable target sights, and a match trigger tuned to break at 1.2kg. Kang-Petrov markets it as a 'training multiplier' — the idea that shooters who practice weekly with the Sport and shoot their duty weapon monthly will outperform shooters who practice monthly with their duty weapon exclusively.

The weapon has become standard equipment at security contractor training facilities, where recruits fire thousands of rounds through KP-22 Sports before ever touching their issued duty weapons. The cost savings are substantial — .22 LR ammunition costs a fraction of 9mm or .45 ACP — and the training transfer is measurable. Kang-Petrov's research division publishes annual data showing accuracy improvements in duty-weapon qualification scores for shooters who train primarily on the Sport.

Kang-Petrov Arms KP-45 Tactical 'Sledge'#

The Kang-Petrov KP-45 Tactical is the heavy-caliber variant of the ubiquitous KP platform, chambered in .45 ACP with a threaded barrel, suppressor-height sights, and an accessory rail. The frame is wider than the standard KP-19, accommodating a double-stack .45 magazine that gives the weapon a distinctly blocky, aggressive profile.

Kang-Petrov designed the Sledge for contract security operators who need more stopping power than 9mm but can't justify the expense of a Volkov-Saito or Arcturus platform. It delivers .45 ACP performance at a price point that bulk purchasers find acceptable, with the same parts-availability advantage that makes the KP-19 so popular. The threaded barrel accepts standard suppressors, making it one of the cheapest suppressor-ready .45 platforms on the market.

The Sledge is the workhorse's bigger, meaner sibling. It lacks refinement but compensates with brute functionality. Security teams who operate in noise-sensitive environments — residential districts, hospital corridors, corporate campuses after hours — favor it for its suppressor compatibility and adequate performance at a fraction of premium pricing.

Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-15 'Diaspora'#

The KPA-15 Diaspora is the most widely manufactured assault rifle on GLMZ. Kang-Petrov Arms designed it for mass production — stamped steel components, minimal machining, and a modular architecture that allows regional factories to produce the weapon with varying levels of sophistication. The base model is a straightforward 5.56mm gas-operated rifle with polymer furniture and a 30-round magazine. Optional BCI-link modules snap into a rail-mounted interface port.

Production variants range from bare-bones militia grade (Φ800) to corporate-contract models with integrated optics and recoil compensation (Φ3,200). This range makes the Diaspora the most democratic weapon in production — it arms everyone from Tier 1 neighborhood watches to Tier 3 corporate auxiliary forces. Kang-Petrov licenses production to fourteen regional manufacturers, ensuring supply even when trade routes collapse.

The weapon's reliability is adequate rather than exceptional, but replacement parts are available everywhere. When a Diaspora breaks, you fix it with parts from any other Diaspora. This interchangeability is its greatest asset and the reason it has proliferated across every conflict zone on the planet.

Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-20E 'Thunderclap'#

Kang-Petrov's first electromagnetic accelerator rifle brings railgun technology to the mass market. The KPA-20E Thunderclap uses a single-stage magnetic acceleration system to fire 3mm steel-core projectiles at supersonic velocity. It lacks the power and range of Arcturus' MAR-8X, but at Φ5,500 it costs less than a quarter of the military platform and requires no BCI integration to operate.

The Thunderclap's capacitor system is integrated into the rifle's stock, providing 40 shots per charge. Recharging takes 120 seconds from a standard power outlet. The weapon has no moving bolt or gas system — projectiles are loaded from a gravity-fed hopper atop the receiver and accelerated through the barrel by electromagnetic coils. This mechanical simplicity means there are no extraction or feeding failures, though the hopper is vulnerable to contamination if left uncovered.

Critics from the premium arms manufacturers dismiss the Thunderclap as a toy — its 3mm projectiles lack the penetration of larger tungsten penetrators, and the single-stage acceleration limits velocity. But for operators who want electromagnetic capability without corporate entanglement, the KPA-20E democratizes access to technology that was previously exclusive to military budgets.

Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-25EM 'Tempest'#

The KPA-25EM Tempest is Kang-Petrov's second-generation electromagnetic rifle, addressing the Thunderclap's limitations with a dual-stage acceleration system and improved capacitor technology. The Tempest fires 4mm tungsten-composite penetrators — an upgrade from the Thunderclap's steel-core rounds — and achieves velocities approaching the Arcturus MAR-8X at two-thirds the cost.

Kang-Petrov's engineering team reverse-engineered the acceleration physics from captured MAR-8X units and developed their own implementation using commercially available components. The Tempest's capacitor system is distributed through the weapon's body rather than concentrated in a single pack, reducing the catastrophic failure risk that plagues Thunderclap modifications. Power supply provides 50 shots per charge with a 60-second recharge cycle.

Arcturus has filed seventeen patent infringement claims against the Tempest, all of which Kang-Petrov has contested in corporate arbitration. The legal battle has become a proxy war over whether electromagnetic weapons technology can be monopolized. Meanwhile, the Tempest ships to any buyer with Φ8,000 and standard licensing.
