Meridian Munitions Peacekeeper-45 'Old Faithful'#

The Meridian Munitions Peacekeeper-45 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .45 ACP using half-moon clips. The weapon is Meridian Munitions' mid-range revolver offering, built with a carbon steel frame and a four-inch barrel. It fills the gap between their bottom-shelf Wheelgun-38 and the premium offerings from Volkov-Saito and Crucible — a functional .45 caliber revolver at a price that working people can afford.

The .45 ACP cartridge in a revolver produces less felt recoil than in a semi-automatic because the revolver's heavier frame and cylinder absorb more energy. This makes the Peacekeeper surprisingly pleasant to shoot for its caliber. The half-moon clips provide a faster reload than individual cartridge loading, and the .45 ACP's subsonic velocity makes it inherently quieter than magnum cartridges — a consideration in residential environments where the Peacekeeper is commonly kept.

Old Faithful earned its nickname through sheer endurance. Meridian Munitions over-builds the Peacekeeper's lockup mechanism relative to the mild pressures of .45 ACP, resulting in a revolver that continues to function accurately long after the cosmetic finish has worn away to bare steel. Multi-generational Peacekeeper owners are not uncommon — families pass down well-worn examples that still shoot straight after decades of use.

Meridian Munitions Precision Carbine MPC-9 'Scalpel'#

The MPC-9 Scalpel is a compact designated marksman rifle designed for urban precision work where a full-length DMR is too cumbersome. The weapon chambers 6.5mm caseless through a 400mm barrel — short for a precision platform — but compensates with a BCI-integrated ballistic computer that wrings maximum accuracy from the abbreviated barrel length. The result is a weapon that delivers 1-MOA accuracy at 600 meters in a package not much larger than a carbine.

Meridian's open-architecture philosophy extends to the Scalpel's optics rail, which accepts any manufacturer's scope or smart-sight. The weapon ships with a basic 1-8x variable optic, but most operators replace it with their preferred precision optic within days. The rifle's compact dimensions allow it to be deployed from vehicle windows, building interiors, and rooftop positions where full-length DMRs are unwieldy.

At Φ6,800, the Scalpel occupies the mid-range of the DMR market. It sacrifices the extreme-range capability of longer-barreled platforms for the versatility of a weapon that functions as both a precision rifle and a fighting carbine. For urban operators who need precision capability without dedicating a team member to a full-size DMR, the MPC-9 provides a compelling compromise.

Meridian Munitions Smart Marksman MSM-5 'Indexer'#

The MSM-5 Indexer is Meridian Munitions' AI-assisted DMR designed to make a competent shooter into a skilled marksman through technology rather than training. The weapon's onboard AI handles windage calculation, range estimation, barometric pressure compensation, Coriolis correction, and spin drift — every variable that a skilled marksman calculates mentally is computed automatically and displayed as a BCI firing solution overlay.

The Indexer fires 6.5mm caseless through a precision barrel and uses Meridian's open-architecture smart-scope interface to connect with any compatible optic. The weapon's AI is the product — the mechanical components are competent but unremarkable. What sets the MSM-5 apart is that it makes 600-meter precision engagement accessible to operators with weeks of training rather than years.

At Φ5,500, the Indexer is positioned as the precision rifle for organizations that cannot afford to invest years in traditional marksman development. Corporate security firms, frontier defense cooperatives, and freelance teams all benefit from fielding operators who can make precision shots without master-level training. Traditional marksmen view the Indexer with contempt. Its users view it with gratitude.

Meridian Munitions Snapper-22 'Cricket'#

The Meridian Munitions Snapper-22 is an eight-shot double-action revolver chambered in .22 LR, built with a lightweight aluminum frame and a three-inch barrel. It is the cheapest revolver Meridian Munitions produces — cheaper even than the Roundhouse — and fills the absolute bottom of the revolver market. The small caliber allows eight rounds in a compact cylinder, giving the Cricket more capacity than most revolvers twice its price.

The Cricket is not a weapon anyone chooses if they have other options. The .22 LR round from a three-inch barrel is marginal for self-defense by any standard, and the aluminum frame feels insubstantial in hand. But the weapon is nearly silent compared to larger calibers, produces virtually no recoil, and costs so little that losing or discarding it carries no financial consequence. These characteristics have made it unexpectedly popular among populations who need a weapon that won't draw attention.

In Shelf districts, the Cricket occupies a specific niche: it is the weapon people carry when they don't want anyone to know they're carrying a weapon. The mild report won't echo through apartment corridors, the small frame disappears in a coat pocket, and the .22 LR round — while weak — is still lethal at the distances that matter in hallways and stairwells.

Meridian Munitions Street PDW MSP-7 'Alleycat'#

The MSP-7 Alleycat is Meridian Munitions' dedicated street-level PDW, designed for the reality of urban self-defense in Tier 2-3 zones. The weapon fires 5.7mm caseless from a 20-round magazine and features Meridian's open-architecture BCI module for operators who have basic neural interfaces. For those without BCI, the weapon includes conventional micro red-dot sights and a manual safety.

The Alleycat's distinguishing feature is its integrated smart-holster system. The weapon's grip contains a biometric lock that releases only for registered users, preventing the weapon from being used against its owner if seized. The holster communicates with the weapon's BCI module to track draw/reholster cycles, and Meridian's companion app provides usage analytics that many operators find useful for training.

At Φ1,800, the Alleycat sits comfortably in the affordable professional range. It is not cheap enough to be disposable or expensive enough to represent an investment. It is a working tool priced for working people — exactly the market Meridian has cultivated. The weapon is reliable without being remarkable, accurate without being precise, and effective without being devastating.

Meridian Munitions Twin PDW MTP-2 'Gemini'#

The MTP-2 Gemini is a paired weapon system — two identical micro-PDWs sold as a matched set and designed to be dual-wielded with BCI coordination. Each unit is a compact 5.7mm caseless PDW with a 15-round magazine, but the weapons' BCI systems communicate to create a unified fire-control solution. When both weapons are drawn, the smart-link allocates targeting between left and right hands, allowing the operator to engage two separate targets simultaneously.

Dual-wielding weapons is generally impractical — human neurology isn't optimized for independent bilateral targeting. The Gemini's BCI system compensates by handling the targeting math neurally, splitting the operator's attention between two aim points and providing independent aim-assist to each hand. The system requires extensive training and a Class 4 motor-interface BCI, but trained Gemini operators can engage two targets in different directions with the speed of a single-weapon draw.

At Φ8,000 per pair, the Gemini is a specialist system for operators with the neural hardware and training to exploit its capabilities. In untrained hands, the paired weapons offer no advantage over a single PDW with a larger magazine. In trained hands, the Gemini doubles the operator's engagement capacity at close range.

Meridian Munitions Urban Carbine MUC-6 'Crosswalk'#

The MUC-6 Crosswalk is Meridian Munitions' urban-optimized carbine, designed for the tight angles, short distances, and civilian density of city combat. The weapon features a short 280mm barrel with aggressive porting that reduces muzzle flash to near-invisible levels in daylight conditions. The integrated BCI link includes a threat-discrimination system that highlights hostile targets in the operator's neural display while tagging bystanders with caution markers.

Chambered in 6mm caseless with an optimized twist rate for close-range terminal performance, the Crosswalk sacrifices ballistic performance beyond 300 meters for devastating effect inside 150. The 6mm round at close range with the Crosswalk's optimized twist fragments reliably in soft tissue while losing energy rapidly after penetration, reducing the risk of overpenetration in populated environments.

Meridian designed the MUC-6 for the urban operators who make up the majority of their customer base — freelancers, security contractors, and bounty hunters whose work happens on city streets, in parking structures, and through apartment corridors. At Φ3,400, the Crosswalk is moderately priced and brutally effective within its intended engagement envelope.

The MVP-3 Sidewinder is Meridian Munitions' compact personal defense weapon, designed for operators who need maximum firepower in minimum space. The weapon uses a telescoping bolt design that wraps around the barrel, reducing overall length to 280mm with the stock folded while maintaining a 180mm barrel for adequate velocity. Chambered in 5.7mm caseless armor-piercing, the Sidewinder punches above its weight class against body armor.

The BCI aim-assist module is the same open-architecture system used in the MM-4 Breadwinner, maintaining Meridian's commitment to non-proprietary accessories. A rail-mounted micro red dot is included as standard, and the weapon accepts any manufacturer's suppressor on its threaded barrel. The 25-round magazine fits flush with the grip, maintaining the compact profile.

At Φ2,200, the Sidewinder occupies the mid-range of the PDW market. It lacks the BCI sophistication of Tessera's Reflex and the rock-bottom pricing of Kang-Petrov's Rattler, but it delivers reliable performance with armor-piercing capability in a package that fits inside a laptop bag. For the freelancer who needs a concealable weapon that can defeat body armor, the MVP-3 is the practical choice.

Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 'Roundhouse'#

The Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .38 Special, built with a carbon steel frame and a four-inch barrel. It is the cheapest revolver available in GLMZ, manufactured using the same cost-minimization approach that defines all Meridian Munitions products. The finish is a flat black oxide that provides minimal corrosion resistance, and the grips are hard rubber with no contouring.

The Roundhouse exists because a significant portion of GLMZ's Shelf population distrusts semi-automatic pistols. Revolvers are mechanically simpler — no magazines to lose, no slides to rack, no safeties to forget. For residents with minimal firearms training, the revolver's simplicity is its primary feature: load it, point it, pull the trigger. The heavy double-action trigger pull serves as both a safety mechanism and a quality-control compromise.

The weapon's reliability is its saving grace. Where a Payday might jam, a Roundhouse will fire. The .38 Special round provides adequate stopping power against unarmored targets, and the six-round cylinder doesn't require counting rounds or managing reloads under stress. For Shelf residents who want 'a gun that works when I need it to work,' the Roundhouse delivers on that promise and nothing more.

Meridian Weartech ShockWeave SW-3 'Thistle'#

A jacket with an electrically conductive outer fabric layer that delivers a 45,000-volt discharge to anyone who grabs the wearer. The ShockWeave system uses a grid of flexible conductive fibers woven into the garment's exterior, connected to a rechargeable battery pack in the jacket's lining. When the wearer activates the system via a switch inside the left sleeve, any firm grip on the jacket's exterior completes a circuit between two conductive zones and delivers a painful shock.

Meridian Weartech designed the SW-3 for people who face frequent physical intimidation — primarily in Tier 1-2 environments where grabbing, pushing, and manhandling are daily hazards. The jacket looks like an ordinary urban outerwear garment; the conductive fibers are indistinguishable from standard fabric to the eye and touch at casual contact. The discharge only triggers with sustained grip pressure above a threshold that eliminates accidental activation from brushing past someone in a crowd.

The SW-3 retails at Φ420 and is rechargeable via a standard wall outlet, providing approximately fifty discharges per charge. The jacket is available in four sizes and two colors (charcoal and black), and the electrical components are removable for washing. Meridian Weartech's warranty explicitly does not cover damage from the wearer being grabbed by multiple attackers simultaneously — the system can deliver to multiple contact points but depletes the battery proportionally.

Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle#

The Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated electromagnetic radiation tuned to the resonant frequency of cytochrome c oxidase — the terminal enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain. On contact, the beam disrupts proton gradient maintenance across the inner mitochondrial membrane, causing a cascading cellular energy failure in targeted tissue within seconds. The effect is not thermal; cells simply cease producing ATP at the required rate, and motor function collapses from the inside out.

What distinguishes the MDPR-2 from comparable disabling weapons is its selectivity and depth of penetration. The beam attenuates predictably through soft tissue but loses minimal energy through non-biological materials, allowing it to affect targets through light cover such as clothing, padding, or standard-grade ballistic weave. Operators describe the effect on unprotected targets as a progressive 'shutdown' — first peripheral muscle groups, then respiratory muscles if exposure is sustained beyond two seconds. Death is possible but requires deliberate extended trigger hold, which gives the weapon plausible deniability as a compliance tool.

Arcturis Defense Solutions markets the MDPR-2 as a 'non-lethal escalation platform,' though this classification is widely contested by independent biomedical researchers and three separate municipal oversight bodies. The weapon is heavy, requires a dedicated power cell rated for thirty shots, and produces a faint violet corona at the emitter aperture that experienced operators call 'the bruise.' Field technicians note that partial cyberware integration — particularly subdermal power cells — can create unpredictable secondary ionization in the target's implants.

Monofilament Whip MFW-1 'Threadkill'#

The MFW-1 is a compact handle unit approximately 18cm long, housing a motorized spool of single-molecule carbon filament 2.4 meters in length. The filament itself is invisible to the naked eye under most lighting conditions, with a weighted ceramic tip that provides gyroscopic stability during movement. When deployed, the filament is capable of passing through soft tissue, most unarmored materials, and commercial-grade polymers without perceptible resistance. The handle includes a tension-feedback system that transmits tactile information about filament contact to the operator's grip, allowing experienced users to feel what the weapon is cutting without visual confirmation.

The MFW-1's primary engineering challenge — and its principal distinction — is filament retrieval. Early monofilament weapons were single-use, as retrieving a molecule-thin cutting edge without severing the operator's fingers required solving a complex tension management problem. The MFW-1 uses a variable-resistance electromagnetic spool with micro-brake segments that progressively decelerate the filament during retraction, guiding it back along a fixed geometric path rather than free-coiling. This allows reliable retrieval in approximately 1.8 seconds, making follow-up strikes viable within the same engagement.

The weapon is extraordinarily dangerous to untrained users and bystanders alike — the filament is effectively invisible in low light and produces no sound during flight. Several documented incidents involve operators accidentally severing their own fingers or limbs during botched retrieval sequences. TESSERA CORPONATION includes a mandatory certification requirement in the purchase contract, though enforcement of this requirement is understood to be nominal.

Myelin Shunt Induction Carbine MSIC-3 'Stutterbox'#

The MSIC-3 operates by projecting a narrow-band oscillating magnetic field tuned precisely to the resonant frequency of myelin sheaths — the insulating protein layers wrapped around peripheral nerve fibers. At sufficient intensity, the field induces rapid localized depolarization cascades along motor neurons, causing involuntary and chaotic muscular contraction. The effect is not pain in the conventional sense but rather a catastrophic loss of motor coherence: targets seize, drop objects, and collapse without any damage to underlying tissue.

What distinguishes the Stutterbox from simpler neuromuscular disruptors is its precision calibration system, which uses a passive biometric ranging ping to adjust field frequency on the fly based on estimated target mass and neural density. This allows it to be effective across a wider range of targets — including partially augmented individuals whose peripheral nervous systems remain biological. Heavily cyberized targets with full neural sleeve replacements are largely immune, a limitation that has shaped how the weapon is tactically deployed.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the MSIC series as a non-lethal compliance tool for corporate security detachments operating in civilian-dense environments. The 'Stutterbox' nickname emerged from enforcement footage that leaked onto GLMZ's underground feeds — the stuttering, marionette-like collapse of targets became darkly iconic, and the weapon's reputation for leaving victims humiliated but unharmed made it paradoxically popular with both law enforcement and certain criminal organizations who prefer leverage over corpses.

Myoelectric Seizure Projector MSP-6 'Marionette'#

The MSP-6 projects a directed myoelectric interference field that hijacks the motor neuron signaling pathway between the brain and skeletal muscle. Rather than inducing pain or unconsciousness, the Marionette intercepts and overrides voluntary muscle control signals, replacing them with a looping pattern of contradictory activation commands. The result is that the target remains fully conscious and cognitively intact while their body ceases to obey them — muscles fire in cycling, uncoordinated patterns dictated by the weapon's signal rather than the target's nervous system. Subjects typically fall, convulse rhythmically, or freeze in a rigid isometric contraction depending on the signal pattern selected.

Ringo Corponation developed the MSP-6 under a contract for a private correctional facility operator seeking alternatives to chemical restraint. The three signal patterns available on the production model — Collapse, Freeze, and Puppet — were each refined through extensive testing that Ringo has declined to document publicly. The Puppet setting, which produces the unsettling rhythmic full-body convulsion that gives the weapon its street name, was reportedly developed for 'aversion compliance training' applications. The weapon found its way out of the correctional supply chain within 18 months of production beginning.

The MSP-6 is uniquely disturbing in that it leaves targets cognitively present throughout the experience — unlike unconsciousness-inducing weapons, subjects remember exactly what happened to their body. Psychological trauma rates among MSP-6 exposure victims are significantly higher than among victims of physically comparable weapons, a fact that is considered a feature by some users. Targets with motor cortex augmentations or neural signal amplifiers are at elevated risk of prolonged effect, as the weapon's field interacts with the amplified signal environment in unpredictable ways.

Myofascial Thermobaric Dispersal Rocket#

The Myofascial Thermobaric Dispersal Rocket uses a two-stage warhead in which the first stage aerosolizes a proprietary fluorocarbon compound tuned to the thermal absorption spectrum of subcutaneous fascia, and the second stage ignites the cloud with a piezoelectric spark array. The resulting deflagration couples preferentially with the fascia layer rather than the surrounding air, meaning targets within the cloud experience an interior burn — heat propagating inward through fascial planes — rather than external flame damage. Structures, vehicles, and equipment in the blast radius show minimal thermal scarring.

The MTDR-9 was developed under a classified ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC contract originally framed as a search-and-rescue tool for locating trapped individuals via their thermal signature — the fluorocarbon compound was initially designed to enhance thermal imaging contrast. The weaponization was a downstream application that ZHENG-DAO has consistently denied. The rocket uses a standard 72mm launch tube compatible with widely distributed civilian construction demolition launchers, giving it an uncomfortable degree of accessibility.

In the field, operators describe targets hit by the MTDR-9 as 'sealed' — the fascial burn creates a subcutaneous compartmentalization effect that traps fluid and heat, producing a characteristic swelling pattern. The weapon's street name, 'Peel-and-Seal,' references this effect. Medical responders require specialized protocols to treat MTDR-9 casualties, as standard burn treatment worsens the compartmentalization.

Nano-Filament Dispersal Unit NFDU-6 'Threadbare'#

The NFDU-6 deploys a compressed canister payload of approximately 40,000 monofilament-gauge carbon-nanotube threads, each between 2 and 8 centimeters in length, suspended in a rapidly evaporating aerosol carrier. Upon detonation, the carrier disperses the threads in a roughly spherical cloud 6 meters in diameter that hangs in the air for 8–12 seconds before the threads settle. Any exposed biological tissue moving through the cloud at typical human speed contacts the threads with enough relative velocity to drive them into the skin, where they become embedded. The threads themselves cause only minor immediate irritation — the real effect is on cybernetic systems. Each thread is coated with a piezoelectric polymer that generates a micro-current on flexion, and embedded in sufficient density around a cybernetic joint or implant housing, they create constant low-level signal interference that degrades fine motor control and causes sensory implants to misfire.

Neural Disruption Charge NDC-7 'Brainstorm'#

The NDC-7 is an electromagnetic pulse device engineered specifically to target neural interface hardware rather than physical infrastructure, developed jointly by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric and Helix Biosystems under a defense contract that was quietly terminated after field trials produced unacceptable civilian casualty rates. The device detonates in two stages: an initial kinetic micro-burst clears a small physical radius, followed immediately by a precisely tuned electromagnetic pulse optimized for the frequency signatures of common neural interface chipsets. Operators with standard neural augmentation within 12 meters experience anything from temporary sensory disruption to catastrophic interface cascade — a condition colloquially called 'brainstorm,' in which the implant attempts to process the pulse as input data and floods the user's sensory cortex with recursive error signals.

Neural Disruption Pistol NDP-4 'Stutter'#

The NDP-4 fires a dart-delivered neural feedback payload: a 2mm tungsten needle carrying a microscale piezoelectric transceiver and a burst-charge of neurotransmitter-disrupting polymer gel. On impact — typically at ranges under 40 meters — the needle embeds in soft tissue and the piezoelectric element activates from the kinetic impact, generating a localized electrical field that destabilizes sodium-channel gating in nearby motor neurons. The polymer gel simultaneously releases a fast-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor into the surrounding tissue, creating a 3-6 second window of profound motor disruption — the target experiences inability to initiate voluntary movement while remaining fully conscious. The effect is colloquially described as 'being frozen mid-thought.'

The NDP-4 uses a neural feedback loop architecture originally developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS for surgical tremor suppression. In its weapons application, the same feedback principle that once stabilized a surgeon's hands is inverted: the transceiver reads the target's local neural activity and generates counter-phase interference signals that scramble motor command transmission. This active interference component extends the disruption window beyond what the chemical payload alone would produce, and means the effect duration varies with the target's neural architecture — individuals with cybernetic motor augmentation may experience shorter disruption (1-2 seconds) or, in documented cases, a paradoxical amplification effect where the augmentation systems attempt to compensate and produce involuntary movement cascades instead.

The pistol itself is compact and conventionally shaped, operating on a CO2-driven dart projector with a 6-round rotary cylinder. Each dart is individually sealed in a nitrogen-purged capsule to preserve the polymer gel payload. The weapon produces minimal sound — a soft pneumatic pop — and no visible projectile, which has made it a favorite of abduction and interrogation specialists who need a target incapacitated without permanent damage and without witnesses understanding what just happened.

Neural Feedback Carbine NFC-3 'Mirrorgun'#

The NFC-3 does not fire a conventional projectile. It emits a tightly focused stream of encoded neural feedback signals derived from the operator's own nervous system, sampled in real time through a sensor array embedded in the grip and stock. The signal stream is amplified, phase-inverted, and projected at the target via a coherent electromagnetic emitter in the barrel. When the stream contacts a target with active neural augmentation — cybernetic nervous system components, neural interface implants, or synaptic enhancement hardware — it creates a feedback loop between the target's augmentation and the projected signal, producing effects ranging from temporary motor disruption to complete neurological shutdown depending on the intensity setting and the target's augmentation profile.

Ringo Corponation developed the NFC-3 as a counter-augmentation platform, responding to the tactical problem of heavily cyberware-augmented combatants who could shrug off conventional firearms due to pain suppression systems and reflex enhancements. The feedback loop exploits the fundamental architecture of neural augmentation: the more extensively a target is augmented, the more vulnerable they are to a correctly tuned feedback stream. Against fully unaugmented targets, the NFC-3 is almost entirely ineffective — the emitted signal has no neural hardware to interact with and dissipates without meaningful effect. This limitation is the weapon's defining tactical characteristic.

The grip sensor array must maintain contact with the operator's bare skin to sample the neural signal baseline. Operators wearing full gloves cannot use the weapon effectively — a deliberate design choice that Ringo Corponation defends as a safety feature preventing unauthorized use, though critics note it also makes the weapon impractical in environments requiring full protective equipment. The weapon's emitter produces a faint violet luminescence during discharge that is invisible to standard optics but detectable to augmented visual systems — a cruel irony given the weapon's primary target demographic.

Neural Resonance Surveillance and Suppression Drone NRSSD-1 'Shepherd'#

The NRSSD-1 is a medium-altitude surveillance and non-lethal suppression drone developed by Ringo Corponation's contested-space management division. At 90 centimeters in rotor diameter, the Shepherd is larger than most urban drones, designed to loiter visibly above crowds, transit zones, and public gatherings. Its primary sensor suite combines optical, thermal, and a low-power neural resonance scanner that can detect elevated stress hormones, rapid heartrate, and adrenaline-response biomarkers in individuals within a 15-meter radius — effectively identifying agitated, frightened, or aggressive people in a crowd before any physical action occurs.

When the onboard threat-assessment algorithm flags a target, the Shepherd deploys one of two responses. The first is the 'Calm' mode: a focused neural feedback emitter directs low-frequency electromagnetic pulses at the target's prefrontal cortex, inducing a sensation of drowsiness, reduced urgency, and mild euphoria. The effect is temporary and non-damaging — subjects typically describe it as 'suddenly feeling tired' without understanding why. The second mode, 'Herd,' activates a directed acoustic discomfort emitter targeting the flagged individual specifically, producing a sensation of pressure and low-grade pain that instinctively drives the subject away from the drone's position — effectively steering people through a space without physical contact.

Ringo Corponation markets the Shepherd as a 'crowd harmony platform' and holds contracts with three of GLMZ's transit authorities and one stadium management corporation. The drone's visible presence is deliberately designed — its blue running lights and rounded profile are intended to read as benign surveillance rather than weaponized intervention. Civil liberties researchers who have documented the Shepherd's neural feedback capabilities argue that the distinction is meaningless, and that the drone constitutes unconsented neurological intervention at population scale. Ringo Corponation's public affairs division has not formally responded to this characterization.

Neurochemical Dispersal Grenade#

The NDG-2 is a non-lethal area-denial grenade that disperses a proprietary aerosolized neurochemical agent developed by LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS under contract for GLMZ's crowd management divisions. On detonation, a binary chemical initiator mixes two stable precursor compounds within the grenade body during a 1.2-second reaction phase, generating the active agent — a synthetic GABAergic compound designated LZR-7 — immediately before aerosol dispersal. This binary approach means the grenade can be stored indefinitely without degradation, solving a persistent shelf-life problem in legacy chemical ordnance.

LZR-7 acts on the central nervous system through inhalation and dermal absorption, inducing acute disorientation, short-term anterograde amnesia, and motor coordination failure within 8–15 seconds of exposure. Effects last 12–40 minutes depending on body mass and respiratory rate. The compound is theoretically non-lethal at standard doses, but LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' internal trials — several of which were conducted without subject consent, according to leaked documents — showed a 3–7% fatality rate in subjects with compromised respiratory systems or certain genetic profiles. This data was suppressed.

Neurolytic Swarm Dispersal Drone NSD-7 'Locust'#

The NSD-7 is a mid-tier autonomous dispersal platform roughly the size of a human fist, housing a compressed micro-swarm of 400–600 semi-independent sub-drones, each no larger than a fingernail. Upon release, the parent chassis identifies thermal signatures within a programmable radius and detonates its swarm canister, sending sub-units in ballistic arcs calibrated to maximize coverage across irregular terrain. Each sub-drone carries a micro-filament electrode array capable of delivering targeted neurolytic pulses to exposed skin or thin fabric.

What distinguishes the NSD-7 from earlier swarm platforms is its use of distributed piezoelectric power harvesting — each sub-drone recharges its discharge capacitor from ambient vibration and pressure as it lands or crawls across a target's body, meaning a single deployment can sustain harassment for up to eighteen minutes without an external power source. The parent drone also maintains a low-frequency coordination signal that prevents sub-units from clustering inefficiently, spreading them in optimized interference patterns across multiple targets simultaneously.

In practice, the NSD-7 does not kill. It overwhelms. Targets experience cascading muscle convulsions, disorientation, and involuntary vocalization as sub-drones fire in coordinated sequences designed to prevent neurological adaptation. Crowd control units favor it for its deniability — sub-drones are difficult to collect as evidence and degrade in UV light within 36 hours.

Neuromorphic Intercept Drone NID-6 'Shepherd'#

The NID-6 is a pursuit-class drone designed to intercept augmented targets and establish a forced neural feedback loop through close-proximity broadcast. Roughly the size of a clenched fist, the Shepherd operates at extreme speed—reaching 140 km/h in short bursts—to close distance with a fleeing target before deploying a focused neuromorphic broadcast array at ranges under two meters. The broadcast generates synthetic neural noise tuned to the target's detected implant signature, overwhelming voluntary motor control and inducing a temporary dissociative state lasting 8–25 seconds depending on augmentation density.

The Shepherd's most technically sophisticated feature is its implant signature library, updated via encrypted uplink to HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' proprietary neural architecture database. Before deploying its broadcast, the drone spends approximately 1.2 seconds in passive scan mode, identifying the specific neural interface architecture present in the target and selecting the most effective noise profile from its library. Heavily augmented targets with multiple neural systems experience compounding disruption as the drone sequences through overlapping broadcast frequencies. Unaugmented targets experience moderate disorientation and nausea but are largely resistant to the motor control effects.

Helix Biosystems markets the NID-6 as a 'compliance assistance platform' for corporate security and law enforcement, emphasizing its non-lethal profile and selective efficacy. Critics—particularly advocacy groups representing augmented citizens—argue that a weapon specifically designed to be more effective against augmented people represents a form of targeted discrimination, and the Shepherd has become a flashpoint in ongoing debates about augmentation rights in GLMZ.

Neuromorphic Pressure Cestus#

The Neuromorphic Pressure Cestus is a combat glove system developed by Tessera Corponation's advanced human-machine interface division, representing a convergence of their proprietary neural feedback architecture with conventional close-combat augmentation. The cestus consists of a form-fitting composite glove with an embedded neuromorphic processing layer — a thin-film synthetic neural network printed directly onto the glove's inner surface and in direct contact with the operator's skin. This network reads the operator's own motor intention signals at the skin surface level, predicting the trajectory and timing of a strike approximately 80 milliseconds before the operator's conscious mind finalizes the movement.

This predictive capability feeds into the cestus's reactive systems: a network of micro-pneumatic pressure cells distributed across the striking surfaces inflates and reconfigures in the 80-millisecond window before impact, dynamically reshaping the glove's contact geometry to maximize force transmission for the specific strike type being thrown. A hook, a straight, an elbow, a palm strike — each receives a different pressure cell configuration optimized for that movement's biomechanical profile. The result is a weapon that makes the operator's natural fighting instincts more effective, rather than requiring them to learn a new system.

Tessera Corponation markets the NPC-1 as 'augmentation that learns you,' and the marketing is largely accurate — the neuromorphic layer adapts over approximately forty hours of use, progressively refining its model of the specific operator's motor patterns. An NPC-1 calibrated to one user is measurably less effective in another's hands, a feature Tessera frames as personalization but which has significant implications for theft, transfer, and the black market.

Tessera Corponation is aware of this market and has been accused of doing nothing because the data itself is commercially valuable.

Nimbus Security ShockRing NR-1 'Kiss'#

A self-defense ring containing a miniaturized capacitor and twin needle electrodes concealed beneath a decorative bezel. When the wearer rotates the bezel 90 degrees with their opposite hand, the electrodes extend 3mm from the ring's surface, and a slap or grab delivers a 40,000-volt discharge directly into the attacker's skin. The discharge is sufficient to cause involuntary release of a grip, a sharp pain response, and a brief moment of muscle spasm — enough to break free from a grab and create space.

Nimbus Security designed the NR-1 specifically for scenarios where the victim has already been grabbed — a wrist seized, an arm held, a shoulder gripped. In these situations, the ring's electrodes are already in contact with the attacker, and activation is immediate. The ring is available in sizes 5 through 13 and in three metals: surgical steel (Φ95), titanium (Φ140), and a gold-plated variant (Φ260) that is functionally identical but aesthetically premium.

The NR-1 holds eight discharges per charge and recharges via a magnetic contact cradle included with purchase. Its limitation is power — at 40,000 volts with extremely low amperage, it causes pain and surprise but does not incapacitate. Nimbus is explicit in their marketing that the NR-1 buys you one second, and what you do with that second determines the outcome.

Nimbus Security WristSafe WS-5 'Viper'#

A chunky fashion bracelet integrating three self-defense functions: a 60,000-volt contact stun, a short-range pepper spray cartridge (single burst, 1.5-meter range), and a GPS-linked distress beacon that transmits the wearer's location to emergency contacts. The WS-5 is activated by voice command, specific wrist gestures, or a hidden button sequence, with each function mapped to a different activation method to prevent accidental deployment.

Nimbus Security positioned the WS-5 as a comprehensive personal safety ecosystem compressed into a wearable form factor. The bracelet's exterior is brushed stainless steel with inlaid composite panels that conceal the spray nozzle, stun electrodes, and antenna. The pepper spray cartridge is a sealed, replaceable module that clicks into the bracelet's inner housing — Nimbus sells refill cartridges at Φ20 each. The stun function recharges wirelessly, and the distress beacon uses the wearer's phone connection for transmission.

The WS-5 retails at Φ520, making it a mid-tier investment. Nimbus markets it through fashion-forward channels, partnering with GLMZ style influencers who normalize wearing it as an accessory rather than a weapon. The bracelet has become popular among young professionals who want comprehensive protection without carrying multiple devices. Its main limitation is the single-burst pepper spray — once deployed, that function is unavailable until the cartridge is replaced.

Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-22 'Peacemaker'#

The Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-22 is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in .22 LR, designed as a training weapon and low-threat personal defense option. The frame is lightweight polymer with a full-size grip designed to approximate the dimensions of common duty pistols, allowing new shooters to build muscle memory that transfers to larger weapons. The recoil is negligible, and the report is mild enough to shoot without ear protection in open environments.

Nkomo-Lindqvist is a small South African-Scandinavian partnership that specializes in the training and recreational market — a niche that larger manufacturers consider beneath their attention. The NL-22 is their flagship product, sold in bulk to shooting ranges, security training academies, and civilian firearms education programs throughout the Mids.

The Peacemaker's name is slightly ironic — the .22 LR round is the least threatening caliber available in a semi-automatic pistol, and carrying one for self-defense is generally regarded as only marginally better than carrying nothing. Nonetheless, the NL-22 has a small but devoted following among people who believe that any gun you can shoot accurately is better than a powerful gun you can't.

Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-9SD 'Lullaby'#

The Nkomo-Lindqvist NL-9SD is a semi-automatic pistol chambered in 9x19mm subsonic, equipped with a detachable suppressor and designed for the civilian self-defense market. Unlike military-grade suppressed weapons, the Lullaby prioritizes ease of use over maximum sound reduction — the suppressor threads on with a quarter-turn, the subsonic ammunition is clearly marked with blue-tip identification, and the manual includes a section titled 'Why Quiet Matters at Home.'

Nkomo-Lindqvist designed the Lullaby for a specific customer: apartment dwellers in Mid-tier residential blocks who want a home defense weapon that won't deafen their family or penetrate into the neighbor's unit. The subsonic 9mm round has enough stopping power for home defense while reducing the risk of over-penetration through interior walls. The suppressor brings the report down to a level that won't cause permanent hearing damage in an enclosed room.

The weapon has been moderately successful in its target market, though it attracts criticism from both directions — firearms enthusiasts dismiss it as a marketing gimmick that wraps a mediocre pistol in a suppressor to justify a premium price, while anti-weapons advocates argue that normalizing suppressor ownership in residential contexts is irresponsible. Nkomo-Lindqvist responds that protecting hearing during a home defense incident is simply sensible design.

Nkomo-Lindqvist NLR-9 'Counselor'#

The Nkomo-Lindqvist NLR-9 is a seven-shot double-action revolver chambered in 9x19mm using moon clips, designed for shooters who want revolver reliability with the ammunition availability and cost savings of the world's most common pistol cartridge. The frame is compact stainless steel, the barrel is three inches, and the overall size is comparable to a medium-frame .38 Special revolver despite holding an additional round.

The Counselor appeals to a practical-minded demographic: people who recognize that 9x19mm ammunition is available everywhere, costs less than revolver-specific cartridges, and performs adequately for personal defense. The moon-clip loading system allows reasonably fast reloads, and the seven-round capacity provides one more round than most .38 Special revolvers. Nkomo-Lindqvist markets the NLR-9 as 'the sensible revolver' — boring marketing for a sensible product.

The weapon has found particular success among medical professionals, social workers, and other non-combat personnel who work in dangerous districts and want reliable personal protection without the learning curve of a semi-automatic pistol. The revolver's simple operation — load, point, pull — combined with universally available ammunition creates a package that prioritizes accessibility over performance.

Nkomo-Lindqvist NLS-20 'Peacekeeper'#

The Nkomo-Lindqvist NLS-20 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 20 gauge designed specifically for civilian home defense, with a built-in trigger lock, a loaded-chamber indicator, and a manual that emphasizes safe storage and handling with the same intensity that other manufacturers dedicate to performance specifications. The barrel is 18 inches with a fixed improved-cylinder choke optimized for buckshot patterning at room distance.

The NLS-20 continues Nkomo-Lindqvist's philosophy of building firearms for people who need protection but aren't firearms enthusiasts. The pump action is deliberately stiff when new — requiring firm, deliberate operation that prevents short-stroking — and loosens to a smooth cycle after a few hundred rounds. The loaded-chamber indicator glows orange when a round is present, visible in darkness without any external light source.

The Peacekeeper competes directly with the Homestead-12 and the Housekeeper for home defense buyers, differentiating on safety features rather than price or performance. Nkomo-Lindqvist's marketing targets households with children, emphasizing the trigger lock, the visible chamber indicator, and the comprehensive safe-handling guide. The weapon is marginally more expensive than competitors but appeals to the safety-conscious demographic that values these features.

NovaTread CaltroDisk CD-1 'Scatterfoot'#

A palm-sized disc that, when thrown on the ground, breaks apart into eighteen spring-loaded micro-caltrops that scatter across approximately four square meters of surface. Each micro-caltrop is a 2-centimeter tetrahedral spike made of hardened polymer — sharp enough to puncture standard footwear soles and embed in the foot, but designed to break off at the base rather than cause deep penetration wounds. The intent is to make pursuit painful and slow rather than to cause serious injury.

NovaTread developed the CD-1 specifically for the 'run and scatter' self-defense scenario — the user throws the disc behind them while fleeing, forcing the pursuer to either stop, navigate around the caltrop field, or step through it and suffer multiple foot punctures. The caltrops are bright orange, making them visible enough that a cautious pursuer will slow down to avoid them, while a reckless pursuer will hit several at full speed.

The CD-1 is sold in packs of two for Φ40. NovaTread includes a small collection magnet in each pack for retrieval of deployed caltrops — the polymer construction means they are not ferromagnetic, but each caltrop contains a small iron bead for magnetic cleanup. GLMZ municipal codes require deployed caltrops to be collected within one hour to avoid hazard to pedestrians, a regulation that is effectively unenforceable given the circumstances under which they are typically deployed.

NullPoint Technologies CortexVeil CV-1 'Silence'#

A self-defense headband that creates a personal electromagnetic cocoon around the wearer's own neural interface, protecting against external BCI intrusion attempts. Unlike NullPoint's offensive products that disrupt attackers' augmentations, the CV-1 is purely defensive — it generates a precisely calibrated interference pattern that blocks unauthorized wireless access to the wearer's BCI without disrupting the interface's normal function.

The CV-1 addresses a growing threat in GLMZ: neural hacking. As BCI technology has become ubiquitous, so have tools for wireless BCI intrusion — devices that can access a victim's neural interface to inject sensory hallucinations, read surface thoughts, trigger pain responses, or disable motor control. These attacks are difficult to detect and nearly impossible to defend against without hardware-level protection. The CV-1 provides that protection in a wearable form factor.

The headband uses a thin conductive mesh that, when powered, generates a white-noise electromagnetic shell around the wearer's cranial BCI hardware. This shell is transparent to the wearer's own BCI signals (which are calibrated during a one-time setup process) but blocks external signals that don't match the authorized pattern. The CV-1 costs Φ450 and is available in several widths and fabric covers to blend with different styles. NullPoint's marketing for the CV-1 is notably more mainstream than their offensive products — protecting your own brain is a less controversial proposition than disrupting someone else's.

tactical use Wear continuously when in public spaces. The CV-1 provides passive protection against wireless BCI intrusion without requiring activation or attention. The one-time calibration process ensures the headband does not interfere with normal BCI function. If you suspect an active intrusion attempt, the CV-1's indicator LED (hidden on the inner surface) will pulse red. In environments where neural hacking is common, wearing the CV-1 is not optional — it is baseline security hygiene.
cultural context The CV-1 has become the BCI equivalent of a condom — protection so obvious that not using it is considered reckless. The street nickname 'Neural Condom' captures both the protective function and the cultural normalcy of the device. In augmented communities, wearing a CV-1 or equivalent is expected, and not wearing one is seen as either naive or inviting trouble. NullPoint's success with the CV-1 has spawned an entire category of 'neural hygiene' products, but the CV-1 remains the market leader.
story hooks
  • A flaw in the CV-1's calibration process has been discovered — if exploited during setup, an attacker can register their own signal pattern as 'authorized,' gaining permanent undetected access to the wearer's BCI through the very device meant to protect it.
  • A Tier 1 community health program is distributing free CV-1 units to augmented residents — but the units were donated by an anonymous corporate sponsor, raising questions about whether the headbands contain a backdoor.

NullPoint Technologies NeuroGuard NG-1 'Static'#

A pendant-sized device that generates a localized electromagnetic interference field designed to disrupt BCI communications within a two-meter radius. The NG-1 does not damage augmentations — it creates a zone of signal noise that degrades the wireless protocols used by neural interfaces to communicate with external systems. For attackers relying on BCI-coordinated combat augmentations, reflex-enhancement systems, or wirelessly linked targeting assists, the NG-1's interference field introduces lag, dropped connections, and phantom inputs that severely degrade their performance.

NullPoint Technologies is a small GLMZ firm founded by former neurosecurity researchers who recognized that the proliferation of combat-grade BCI augmentations among street-level criminals had created a defensive gap for unaugmented citizens. The NG-1 is their flagship product: affordable BCI disruption for people who cannot afford BCI augmentations of their own. The device is worn on a cord around the neck and activated by pressing a button on its face.

The NG-1's interference field is indiscriminate — it affects all BCI communications within range, including the user's own augmentations if they have them, and the augmentations of innocent bystanders. This has generated controversy, as the device can disrupt medical-grade neural interfaces (pain management, seizure prevention, mood regulation) in addition to combat augmentations. NullPoint's legal defense — that the device is no different from a radio jammer in principle — has not satisfied augmented rights advocates. The NG-1 retails for Φ190.

NullPoint Technologies SynapseJam SJ-3 'Migraine'#

A directed BCI disruption device that fires a focused electromagnetic pulse calibrated to the operating frequencies of common neural interface models. Unlike the omnidirectional NG-1, the SJ-3 is a point-and-shoot device that delivers its disruption field in a narrow cone, affecting only the targeted individual within a five-meter range. The SJ-3's pulse causes a brief but intense disruption of BCI signal processing, manifesting as a 'neural stutter' — a two-to-four-second window during which augmented cognitive functions (enhanced reflexes, threat assessment, sensory processing) experience cascading errors.

The SJ-3 represents NullPoint's second-generation BCI defense technology, incorporating frequency profiles for the forty most common neural interface models in GLMZ. The device automatically scans for BCI signal emissions and adjusts its disruption pulse to match the detected interface's operating frequency, significantly increasing effectiveness compared to the broadband interference of the NG-1. This targeting capability also means the SJ-3 is less likely to affect bystanders' augmentations — though it will still disrupt any BCI system within its cone.

Priced at Φ680, the SJ-3 is a significant investment but has found a market among individuals who have been specifically victimized by augmented criminals and are willing to invest in targeted countermeasures. NullPoint sells the device through security consultants rather than retail channels, partly for liability management and partly to ensure purchasers receive training in appropriate use.

Osmotic Cranial Pressure Induction Rifle OCPIR-3 'Headwater'#

The OCPIR-3 operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated osmotic-induction radiation that penetrates the skull and disrupts the choroid plexus — the brain tissue responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid. The beam artificially accelerates CSF production while simultaneously inducing localized vasoconstriction in the arachnoid granulations, blocking the fluid's reabsorption pathway. Within seconds, intracranial pressure begins to climb, causing escalating symptoms ranging from blinding headache and visual distortion to projectile vomiting and loss of motor control. At sustained exposure, the effect becomes life-threatening.

What distinguishes the Headwater from cruder neural-targeting weapons is its precision gradient control. Operators can dial the induction intensity to achieve calibrated non-lethal incapacitation — a target left writhing but intact — or ramp the beam to levels that risk cerebral herniation. This tunability made it enormously attractive to corporate security contractors who needed a weapon that could be justified in court as 'non-lethal deployment' while still carrying the implicit threat of a lethal setting.

The weapon is built on a long-barreled platform resembling an anti-materiel rifle, fitted with a large-aperture emitter dish that gives it an unmistakable silhouette. Users report that targets struck at mid-range settings describe the experience as 'the worst migraine of my life followed by not knowing where my legs were.' Street medics in GLMZ's lower tiers have learned to recognize the presentation and carry emergency hypertonic saline kits as a field countermeasure.

Osmotic Pressure Blade#

The Osmotic Pressure Blade is a combat knife developed by Helix Biosystems as a counterintelligence and targeted neutralization tool, distinguished by its hollow ceramic blade construction and an integrated osmotic delivery system embedded in the handle. The blade is permeated by a network of semi-permeable micro-channels connected to a pressurized reservoir in the grip. Upon penetration of biological tissue, the weapon's passive osmotic differential — established by a hyperosmotic solution in the reservoir — draws interstitial fluid from the wound site inward while simultaneously pushing a controlled dose of the reservoir compound outward through the channel network and into the surrounding tissue.

The genius of the OPB-3's design is that it does not rely on injection mechanisms or active pumps — the osmotic differential does the work, and the deeper the blade is seated in tissue, the greater the exchange rate. The reservoir compound is user-configurable: Helix Biosystems offers a proprietary line of combat-grade solutions ranging from rapid coagulants (designed for field surgery applications, the weapon's official cover purpose) to vasoactive compounds, neural disruptors, or custom biologics available through licensed Helix channels. The blade's ceramic construction makes it invisible to standard metal detection, and the reservoir is shielded against spectroscopic surface scanning.

In the field, operators describe the OPB-3 as 'a knife that doesn't stop working after you pull it out' — the osmotic compound continues diffusing through tissue for minutes to hours after a wound is closed, depending on the formulation used. This temporal displacement between the act of stabbing and the onset of the compound's effects has made the OPB-3 a favored tool for operations requiring deniability.

Osmotic Pressure Injection System OPIS-1 'Skindeep'#

The OPIS-1 'Skindeep' is a short-to-medium range delivery weapon developed by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals that uses focused osmotic pressure waves to drive liquid payloads through intact skin and soft tissue without penetrating the surface — no needle, no wound, no visible mark. The weapon generates a precisely calibrated pressure differential at the target surface, temporarily increasing cellular membrane permeability in a localized area and forcing a liquid payload carried in the weapon's pressurized reservoir through the skin barrier and into subcutaneous or intramuscular tissue. The payload — which can be any compound stable in liquid suspension — is delivered in approximately 0.3 seconds and leaves no external evidence of administration beyond a brief, easily-missed reddening of the skin.

Osseoconductive Fracture Hammer OFH-1 'Inheritance'#

The OFH-1 is a compact single-handed impact weapon — visually similar to a geological survey hammer — with a striking face constructed from a piezoelectric transducer array embedded in a dense tungsten carbide head. On impact with bone or bone-equivalent material (including certain ceramic augmentation components), the transducer array reads the resonant frequency of the target structure and, within a single millisecond, fires a return pulse tuned to that structure's harmonic failure frequency. The effect is not merely blunt trauma — it is a precisely engineered fracture event in which the target bone is induced to shatter along its own crystalline stress lines rather than simply breaking under compressive force.

The distinction matters enormously in practice. A conventional hammer blow to a forearm might fracture the ulna in one or two places. The OFH-1's resonance-matched pulse propagates the fracture event along the entire bone simultaneously, producing a catastrophic multi-point failure that is both more immediately disabling and far more difficult to surgically repair. The wave propagation also travels through connected bone structures — a strike to the wrist can produce secondary fracture events in the elbow and shoulder within 0.3 seconds, as the initial resonance pulse travels up the skeletal chain before dissipating. Operators describe this as 'the echo effect.'

OUROBOROS ENERGY originally developed the underlying osseoconductive frequency analysis technology for geological survey work — reading rock strata resonance to identify fracture points before controlled demolition. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION licensed the technology for structural assessment. At some point between those applications and the current one, an unknown party commissioned a weaponized adaptation. The OFH-1 carries no manufacturer's mark, no serial number, and uses a proprietary transducer compound that materials analysis has not definitively sourced. It exists, officially, as an anomaly.

Ossic Resonance Baton ORB-3 'Earbreaker'#

The ORB-3 is a 60cm impact baton constructed from dense polymer composite over a titanium core, with a secondary function as a precision resonance delivery device. The baton's striking surface houses an array of micro-transducers capable of generating targeted ultrasonic pulses at the moment of contact, transmitting vibrational energy directly through struck surfaces — including bone, cartilage, and implant housings — rather than simply delivering blunt kinetic force. A standard impact from the ORB-3 carries the physical effect of the blow plus a concentrated resonance burst that propagates through the target's skeletal structure, inducing acute pain response, joint destabilization, and in repeated strikes, microfracture accumulation in bone density.

The weapon's resonance profile is tunable via a recessed dial at the base of the grip, allowing operators to shift between a bone-conduction pain mode, an inner-ear disruption mode that causes severe vertigo and nausea, and a structural mode intended for use against reinforced materials and door panels. The inner-ear mode is the weapon's most notorious application — a single strike to the shoulder or back of the head can induce complete vestibular disruption lasting between 30 seconds and several minutes, rendering a target unable to stand or orient without causing them any visible external injury.

Helix Biosystems developed the ORB-3 as a crowd-control tool for private security contracts, but the inner-ear mode was discovered and publicized by an independent weapons analyst within a year of launch. The subsequent controversy did not result in the weapon's prohibition but did generate a licensing requirement that is routinely circumvented through intermediary sales.

Ossuary Arms Memento Mori OA-3 'Wake'#

A bolt-action precision rifle built with a deliberately antiquated aesthetic — walnut stock, blued steel, hand-checkered grip — that conceals a modern BCI-integrated firing computer in its stock. Ossuary Arms builds weapons for operators who believe that the act of precision shooting is a craft, not a procedure.

The Wake's BCI integration is minimal and respectful. It provides wind data, range estimation, and a recommended hold point, but it does not guide the round or correct for shooter error. The operator must still execute the shot. Ossuary's founder has been quoted saying 'The machine tells you where to aim. Your hands decide if you are worthy.'

The Memento Mori fires a heavy 10.3mm match round at subsonic velocities through a hand-fitted barrel that achieves sub-MOA accuracy at 1,000 meters. Each rifle is engraved with the name of its first owner and cannot be re-registered.

Ossuary Arms designed the OA-7 as a conceptual weapon — the idea that violence can carry a message is as old as warfare, but the Momento literalizes it. The weapon has found use in psychological warfare, where the content of the data payload is as important as the physical damage. Threats, warnings, demands, and even advertisements have been delivered via Momento round. The weapon has also been used to deliver malware to BCI systems — a round that hacks as it kills.

Ouroboros CS-4 'Gentleman'#

A carbon-fiber walking cane containing a 60-centimeter monomolecular-edged blade concealed within the shaft. The blade is drawn by twisting the cane's handle 90 degrees and pulling — a motion that takes approximately 0.3 seconds for a practiced user. The blade's monomolecular edge can sever unarmored limbs, and the cane's 90-centimeter overall length provides reach advantage over conventional bladed weapons. The remaining shaft section serves as a parrying tool or blunt-force weapon after the blade is drawn.

Ouroboros manufactures the Gentleman for a specific clientele: wealthy individuals in GLMZ's upper tiers who face personal security threats but cannot be seen carrying weapons without damaging their social position. The cane is crafted from genuine carbon fiber with premium fittings, weighted for comfortable walking use, and finished to standards that justify its Φ8,000 price point as a luxury accessory. In a social environment where visible weapons are considered gauche, the Gentleman allows its owner to be armed while appearing civilized.

The weapon's monomolecular edge is its most dangerous feature and its primary maintenance burden. The edge degrades with each use and requires professional resharpening that only Ouroboros-certified technicians can perform. This creates a dependency chain — Gentleman owners must maintain a relationship with Ouroboros to keep their weapon functional, and Ouroboros's maintenance records constitute a database of every person in GLMZ who is carrying a concealed monomolecular blade.

Ouroboros PD-2 'Aegis'#

A double-barreled derringer-format pistol chambered in .410/.45 Colt, capable of firing either shotshells or pistol rounds from its two over-under barrels. The Aegis provides maximum close-range versatility in a package small enough to conceal in an ankle holster — one barrel loaded with a .410 buckshot shell for close-range spread, one with a .45 Colt round for aimed fire. The operator selects which barrel fires first via a barrel-select switch on the frame.

Ouroboros designed the Aegis for people who want a backup weapon that can handle the two most common self-defense scenarios: an attacker at arm's reach (buckshot) and an attacker at room distance (pistol round). The double-barrel design means only two shots before reloading, but the combination of spread and precision in a pocket-sized package has made the Aegis the most popular backup weapon in GLMZ among security professionals and civilians alike.

The weapon's compact dimensions and dual-caliber capability have also made it popular in the Shelf, where .410 shotshells and .45 Colt rounds are among the most commonly available ammunition types. A Φ600 Aegis loaded with one buckshot shell and one .45 round provides a civilian with two different solutions to two different problems, in a weapon that disappears in an ankle holster and weighs less than a can of soda.

Ouroboros SB-1 'Arbalest'#

A vehicle-mounted heavy crossbow platform that fires 1-meter steel bolts weighing 5 kilograms at velocities sufficient to penetrate reinforced concrete walls. The Arbalest uses a hydraulic draw mechanism that charges a bank of torsion springs generating 400 kilograms of draw force, combined with a short electromagnetic acceleration stage that brings the bolt to terminal velocity. The weapon is mounted on a powered gimbal that allows 180-degree traverse and 45-degree elevation from a vehicle roof or fixed position.

Ouroboros developed the Arbalest as a breaching tool for tactical teams that need to penetrate fortified positions without explosive ordnance. A 5-kilogram steel bolt arriving at 200 m/s punches through walls, doors, barricades, and light vehicles with the kinetic energy of a small cannon round, but without the explosive signature, fragmentation hazard, or ammunition regulation of conventional heavy weapons. Like the Longbow, the Arbalest exploits the legal fiction that anything firing a bolt is a crossbow.

The weapon's most common deployment is punching access holes through walls during forced-entry operations — a single Arbalest bolt creates a 15-centimeter breach that operators can use as a firing port, observation point, or anchor for breaching charges. Three bolts in a triangular pattern create a hole large enough for a person to enter. The process is slower than explosive breaching but creates no blast injury risk to occupants the entry team wants alive.

Ouroboros UW-5 'Harpoon'#

A pneumatic speargun designed for underwater combat in GLMZ's flooded infrastructure, submerged transit tunnels, and coastal industrial zones. The UW-5 fires a 30-centimeter steel spear using compressed air at velocities effective to 15 meters underwater — dramatically reduced from surface weapon ranges due to water resistance, but sufficient for the close-quarters engagements that underwater environments demand. The spear is tethered to the weapon by a retractable monofilament line, allowing recovery and reload.

Ouroboros developed the UW-5 because GLMZ has an underwater problem. Decades of subsidence, flooding, and rising water tables have created an extensive network of partially or fully submerged spaces beneath the city — old transit tunnels, basement levels, industrial chambers, and infrastructure corridors that are now accessible only by diving. These spaces are used for smuggling, storage, clandestine manufacturing, and hiding. Conventional firearms are useless underwater; the UW-5 fills the gap.

The weapon's most common deployment is during drainage operations, where security teams must clear flooded spaces that may contain hostile occupants. The UW-5's monofilament tether serves double duty — the spear can be used to anchor to structures for movement in current, and the retraction mechanism provides a crude grappling capability. In the dark, flooded tunnels beneath GLMZ, the UW-5 is the difference between an operator and a drowning victim.

Ouroboros XB-7 'Silence'#

Oxidative Lymphatic Diffusion Injector#

The OLDI-3 is a contact-delivery weapon disguised as a standard medical injector, approximately the size and weight of a thick pen. On skin contact and trigger depression, it delivers a payload of oxidative iron nanoparticle suspension directly through the dermis via high-pressure micro-needle array, bypassing the need for visible puncture or vascular access. The particles enter the lymphatic system and begin a slow oxidative process that progressively degrades lymph node tissue, producing an expanding cascade of immune dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and eventually systemic failure. The process takes between three days and three weeks depending on the payload concentration and the target's biological constitution.

The insidious design intent of the OLDI-3 is temporal dislocation — the weapon is designed to be used in a moment of brief physical contact (a handshake, a crowd brush, a brief struggle) and to produce consequences that emerge long after any connection to that moment can be established. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals developed it under a medical research exemption, ostensibly to study lymphatic drug delivery mechanisms. The weaponized application was, according to company documentation, entirely unintended, a position that has satisfied no investigator who has examined it. The injector contains no moving parts that would register on standard weapons scanners, and the micro-needle array is indistinguishable from a standard dermal patch applicator.

The name 'Rust' describes the slow, inevitable quality of its effect. 'The Long Shake' refers to the handshake delivery method favored by professional operators, and has entered GLMZ's political vocabulary as a term for any arrangement where the consequences of a meeting only become apparent weeks later.

Oxidative Plasma Breath Lance OPBL-1 'Vestment'#

The Oxidative Plasma Breath Lance generates a sustained stream of superheated oxidative plasma through a catalytic compression nozzle, but its defining characteristic is the delivery geometry: rather than a focused jet, the OPBL-1 produces a wide, flat, billowing emission — roughly 1.4 meters wide at three meters range — that operators describe as resembling a thrown cloak or a priest's vestment caught in wind. TESSERA CORPONATION's original design brief called for a weapon capable of simultaneous full-torso surface contact, and the Vestment delivers exactly that, enveloping a target in plasma rather than puncturing them with it.

The oxidative component is key to the weapon's particular lethality. Standard plasma weapons inflict thermal damage; the OPBL-1 additionally saturates the plasma stream with a high-oxygen reactive medium, accelerating combustion on contact with organic materials and causing secondary ignition in clothing, hair, and exposed tissue layers. The effect on armored targets is more nuanced — the flat emission wraps around armor edges, finding gaps at joints and seals, which makes it disproportionately effective against targets whose frontal coverage is strong but whose lateral and rear seals are imperfect. TESSERA markets this as 'coverage-adaptive thermal application.'

The OPBL-1 is a two-handed platform, roughly the dimensions of a combat shotgun, with a distinctive flat-mouthed nozzle resembling a wide letterbox slot. It is slow between emissions — the catalytic chamber requires 4 seconds to re-pressurize — and operators are trained to treat each emission as a decisive action rather than suppressing fire. The weapon's cultural weight comes almost entirely from its visual signature: the billowing plasma 'vestment' is unmistakable at range and has become one of GLMZ's most recognized weapon silhouettes.

Oxidative Thermal Drift Drone OTDD-4 'Ember'#

The OTDD-4 is a persistent area-heating platform developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY's defense subsidiary from industrial thermal management technology originally designed for pipeline thaw operations in extreme cold environments. The drone carries a focused oxidative catalytic emitter — a system that superheats a concentrated column of ambient air through rapid catalytic oxidation cycling rather than combustion, producing a sustained thermal cone that can raise surface temperatures in a 3-meter radius by 40–90 degrees Celsius depending on proximity and dwell time. The effect on organic targets ranges from rapid dehydration and heat exhaustion at range to contact burns and respiratory damage at close quarters.

The OTDD-4 is not a fast weapon. It moves slowly, holds altitude with deliberate stability, and requires 8–12 seconds of dwell time to produce incapacitating effects on an unprotected target. What it offers is persistence and silence — the catalytic emitter produces no flame, no visible beam, and no significant acoustic signature. Targets describe the experience as standing next to an industrial furnace that appeared from nowhere. The drone's thermal signature is, paradoxically, a liability: most military-grade thermal detection systems will acquire it immediately. It was designed for use against targets without such equipment.

OUROBOROS ENERGY's civilian documentation describes the OTDD-4 as an 'ice management and environmental thermal correction platform.' The same hardware, the same firmware, the same catalytic array. The company notes that operational parameters outside intended use cases are the operator's legal responsibility.

Periosteal Galvanic Stress Fracture Emitter#

The Periosteal Galvanic Stress Fracture Emitter directs a focused beam of low-frequency alternating electrical current through the target's skeletal structure using transcutaneous capacitive coupling — no physical contact required. The current is modulated to exploit the piezoelectric properties of bone mineral, inducing microscopic oscillatory stress at the crystalline level of hydroxyapatite within cortical bone. Over a sustained engagement of thirty to ninety seconds, this mechanical fatigue accumulates until spontaneous stress fractures propagate through weight-bearing bones. The tibia and femur are primary targets at standard settings; the weapon can be retargeted to the spinal column with a firmware adjustment.

The PGSFE-3 differs from earlier galvanic bone-disruption concepts in its use of a resonance feedback loop: onboard sensors detect the acoustic signature of the target's bone structure through the return signal, allowing the emitter to continuously tune its frequency to the target's specific bone density and mineral composition. This means the weapon is self-optimizing — it gets more efficient the longer it is applied. An operator who holds a target in the beam for the full ninety-second cycle will typically induce complete bilateral tibial fracture, dropping the target without any surface wound, blood, or external sign of cause.

The emitter requires line-of-sight but penetrates most civilian clothing without attenuation. Thick metal plating — the kind found in high-end combat chassis augmentations — can shield the underlying biological bone, but few civilian-grade augments include full skeletal shielding. The weapon's power draw is substantial, and the emitter head generates significant waste heat, requiring a thirty-second cooling cycle between full engagements.

Periosteal Resonance Targeting Drone PRTD-5 'Knuckle'#

The PRTD-5 is a close-support targeting and area-denial drone developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint contract with military medical research divisions. It operates by emitting narrow-band low-frequency acoustic pulses precisely tuned to periosteal resonance frequencies — the vibrational signature of the membrane sheathing bone. At its standard operational distance of 2–6 meters, these pulses produce deep, nauseating ache in weight-bearing joints: knees, hips, ankles, and wrists. The sensation is not structural damage but reads to the nervous system as imminent catastrophic fracture, producing involuntary protective responses including crouching, freezing, and gait collapse.

The PRTD-5 is distinguished from simpler acoustic deterrents by its precision tracking suite. An onboard millimeter-wave radar maps the target's skeletal geometry in real time, allowing the drone to adjust its emission frequency to match individual bone density — thicker cortical bone requires lower frequencies and higher amplitude. This adaptive tuning means the effect is not trivially countered by body armor or padding, which attenuates higher-frequency acoustic weapons but does relatively little against the PRTD-5's deep-penetration range. The drone is roughly the size and shape of a softball, matte gray, and nearly silent in flight.

ACTARUS markets it officially as a non-lethal crowd management tool for use by licensed security contractors. The military variant, designated PRTD-5M, operates at amplitudes that cause genuine microfracture accumulation over extended exposure — a detail absent from the civilian product documentation.

Peristaltic Compression Rifle PCR-4 'Constrictor'#

The PCR-4 operates by projecting a tightly focused column of oscillating peristaltic pressure waves tuned to the resonant frequency of soft visceral tissue. Unlike blunt trauma weapons that damage through impact, the Constrictor induces rhythmic, involuntary compression cycles in the target's abdominal and thoracic cavities — essentially forcing the body's own musculature to contract violently and out of sequence. At low power, this produces incapacitating nausea, involuntary voiding, and diaphragm spasms that prevent breathing. At full charge, internal organs rupture without any visible external wound.

The weapon was originally developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric as a non-lethal crowd suppression tool for use in enclosed transit corridors and arcology common spaces where conventional ballistic discharge was a structural liability. The lethality at upper power registers was considered an acceptable engineering footnote. The emitter array at the barrel's terminus is a concave dish of piezoelectric transducer cells arranged in a Fibonacci spiral, which focuses the wave column to a diameter of roughly 30 centimeters at optimal range.

What makes the PCR-4 distinctively feared is the nature of the wounds it leaves — or rather, doesn't leave. Forensic examination of victims shows no entry wound, no burning, no fracture. Cause of death reads as catastrophic multi-organ failure, consistent with advanced disease. In jurisdictions with overwhelmed forensic infrastructure, Constrictor kills pass unreported as natural causes with disturbing regularity.
