ShieldTech Tandem Shock Set TSS-2 'Convergence'#

The TSS-2 'Convergence' is ShieldTech's dual-baton system — a matched pair of 45-centimeter short batons designed to be used simultaneously by a trained two-handed operator. Each baton is functional as a standalone shock device, but the system's distinguishing feature is its Synchronized Discharge Architecture (SDA): when both batons contact a target within a 500-millisecond window, the system detects the closed circuit and delivers a coordinated dual-discharge that routes current between the two contact points through the target's body, rather than to ground. This dramatically increases current density through the target's torso and creates a more comprehensive neuromuscular disruption than either baton could achieve independently.

ShieldTech developed the Convergence for close-quarters combat specialists and executive protection operatives who operate in environments where long batons are impractical — vehicle interiors, narrow corridors, elevator confrontations, close-press crowd situations. The short form factor allows both batons to be carried in a dual-hip holster rig or concealed in a jacket's inner pockets. The synchronized discharge requires deliberate two-point contact, which means casual or accidental discharge is less likely than with standard single-baton systems, a safety feature ShieldTech has emphasized in its regulatory filings.

The training requirement for effective dual-baton use is nontrivial — operating two weapons simultaneously while maintaining positional awareness is a skill that requires practice to develop — and ShieldTech offers a certified training program through its authorized dealer network. The Convergence comes with a 'solo mode' that disables SDA and allows each baton to function independently as a standard 130,000-volt device, which most purchasers use until they complete the dual-operator training.

In mainstream culture, the image of two batons lighting up simultaneously has become a visual shorthand in entertainment media for 'elite private security,' appearing in numerous drama series set in the Spire.
known users

  • close-quarters security operatives

story hooks
  • A ShieldTech Convergence training facility has been running unsanctioned night sessions — the discharge logs from the training units show hundreds of unauthorized uses outside business hours, and the biometric enrollment data includes names that match known members of a Tier 3 political organizing group. Someone is running a combat training program for civilians. ShieldTech's internal security is trying to determine whether to report this or quietly erase the logs.

ShieldTech UVTrace UT-1 Identification Spray#

The ShieldTech UT-1 UVTrace is a forensic identification aerosol designed for the rapid, covert tagging of individuals during security incidents. The active compound is a synthetic fluorescent dye — Lumogen Violet LV-7, a ShieldTech proprietary formulation — suspended in a fast-drying alcohol carrier that bonds to skin, hair, and most textile fibers within 8–12 seconds of application. The dye is completely invisible under ambient light but fluoresces intensely at 365nm UV illumination, which is standard in all GLMZ transit authority checkpoints, police processing facilities, and most corporate security screening stations. A single one-second application leaves a UV signature detectable for 48–72 hours on skin and up to two weeks on fabrics, surviving multiple hand-washing cycles.

The UT-1 is marketed to security personnel as a force-multiplier for incident response — rather than attempting to physically detain every individual involved in a disturbance, security operators can quickly spray multiple subjects and allow them to disperse, knowing that the tagged individuals will be automatically flagged when they pass through any UV-equipped security checkpoint in the city. ShieldTech's marketing materials describe it as 'converting a crowd-control problem into a forensic data collection opportunity.' The spray has no biological effect beyond very mild alcohol-carrier dryness and is considered genuinely non-lethal by any meaningful metric.

The UT-1 has, however, generated controversy in civil liberties contexts. Critics point out that the spray effectively converts any security encounter into an extended surveillance operation — a person tagged at a protest can be identified, processed, and potentially prosecuted days later based on their UV signature, even if they were never formally detained. In Tier 1 and 2 zones where UV checkpoints are ubiquitous, there is effectively no way to avoid eventual detection once tagged.

Splanchnic Neural Feedback Disruptor#

The SNFD-1 targets the splanchnic nervous system — the dense network of autonomic nerves governing abdominal organ function — by projecting a modulated neural feedback pulse that overrides normal visceral signaling. The pulse induces simultaneous paradoxical signals across the celiac, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric ganglia: organs receive competing commands to contract and dilate, to accelerate and suppress motility, to activate and inhibit secretion. The result is catastrophic visceral dysregulation — violent involuntary peristalsis, acute nausea and vomiting, loss of bladder and bowel control, and waves of referred pain across the entire abdomen.

The weapon's designers at Ringo Corponation specifically engineered the feedback loop to bypass voluntary nervous system override. Training, pain tolerance, and pharmacological suppressants provide minimal resistance — the splanchnic network is largely inaccessible to conscious control, meaning even highly augmented or conditioned targets respond to the SNFD-1 with full incapacitation. The effect lasts between eight and twenty-five minutes depending on individual physiology, with a lingering period of autonomic instability for up to two hours afterward.

What has made the Gutcheck genuinely feared is its psychological dimension. The profound loss of bodily control it induces — particularly the incontinence — causes acute shame responses that outlast the physical effect. Ringo Corponation's internal testing documentation, leaked in 2183, revealed that the psychological recovery period was considered a 'feature' during development, as targets subjected to the weapon in coercive contexts showed significantly elevated compliance in subsequent interactions. The company has never publicly acknowledged the leak.

Sterling-Nakamura Cascade Projector SN-7 'Monsoon'#

A man-portable electromagnetic suppression system that fires rapid bursts of magnetically-accelerated ceramic slugs. The Monsoon trades the sustained fire capability of conventional machine guns for overwhelming burst density — each trigger pull releases a 40-round burst in 0.3 seconds, creating an instantaneous wall of projectiles.

Sterling-Nakamura designed the Cascade Projector for ambush and counter-ambush scenarios where the first seconds of contact determine the outcome. The SN-7's burst capability allows a single operator to deliver the firepower equivalent of a full squad's opening volley. The ceramic slugs fragment on impact with hard surfaces, producing secondary projectile effects that extend the weapon's lethality beyond its direct fire pattern.

The trade-off is ammunition consumption. A 400-round magazine provides only 10 trigger pulls, and the weapon's electromagnetic accelerator requires a 2-second recharge between bursts. Monsoon operators learn to make each burst count.

Sterling-Nakamura Clarity SN-11 'Glass Eye'#

A precision rifle built around its optics rather than its ballistics. The Clarity SN-11 integrates a multi-spectrum sensor suite that provides the operator with thermal, electromagnetic, and acoustic imaging overlaid onto a BCI-projected heads-up display. The weapon itself fires conventional 6.5mm rounds — it is the targeting system that justifies the price.

Sterling-Nakamura's approach inverts the traditional sniper weapons philosophy. Rather than building a better bullet, they built a better eye. The SN-11's sensor suite can detect targets through walls, identify cyberware signatures from 2km away, and predict target movement using pattern-recognition algorithms that learn from the operator's engagement history.

The Glass Eye has found a niche among intelligence-oriented operators who value the sensor data as much as the weapon's lethality. Some operators reportedly disable the weapon entirely and use the SN-11 purely as a surveillance platform.

Sterling-Nakamura PersonalAegis PA-7 'Rampart'#

A handheld hardlight projector that generates a 60-centimeter-diameter disc of semi-solid photonic matter, functioning as a personal shield capable of deflecting physical blows, absorbing low-velocity projectiles, and blocking chemical sprays. The PA-7 is the first consumer-grade hardlight product, adapted from Sterling-Nakamura's military hardlight barrier systems with drastically reduced power and duration to meet civilian safety standards and battery constraints.

The shield disc projects from a grip-activated emitter roughly the size of a flashlight handle. When activated, the disc materializes in approximately 0.3 seconds and maintains coherence for up to eight seconds per activation, with four activations per charge. The hardlight surface has the approximate stopping power of 6mm polycarbonate — sufficient to block a punch, a knife slash, or a low-velocity flechette round, but not rated against standard firearms ammunition or high-energy weapons.

Sterling-Nakamura prices the PA-7 at Φ2,400, firmly in the Tier 3-4 market segment. The device is marketed through personal security consultants and high-end lifestyle retailers, emphasizing its technological sophistication and the prestige of carrying hardlight technology. The limited eight-second activation window per use means the PA-7 is a reactive tool — something deployed in the critical seconds of an encounter rather than a sustained defensive system.

Sterling-Nakamura Photonic Disruptor SN-15 'Prism'#

A directed energy weapon that fires a multi-frequency laser burst spanning the visible, infrared, and ultraviolet spectrum simultaneously. The Prism's polychromatic beam defeats single-frequency laser countermeasures — reflective armor, frequency-specific filters, and ablative coatings are each designed to counter one wavelength. The SN-15 attacks with all of them at once.

Sterling-Nakamura developed the Photonic Disruptor in response to the proliferation of anti-laser defensive systems. As directed energy weapons became common, defensive technology adapted to counter them. The Prism's multi-frequency approach ensures that no single-spectrum defense can protect against its beam — some wavelengths may be blocked, but others will penetrate.

The weapon produces a visible beam that shifts through the color spectrum during each pulse — a distinctive rainbow effect that has made the Prism instantly recognizable on the battlefield. The visual spectacle is dramatic enough that combat footage of Prism engagements has become iconic in GLMZ's military media culture.

Sterling-Nakamura Subsonic Eliminator SE-9 'Hush'#

A purpose-built suppressed pistol designed from the ground up for silent operation rather than having a suppressor added as an afterthought. The SE-9 uses an integral suppressor barrel, subsonic ammunition with a specialized wipe system, and a locked-breech action that eliminates the mechanical noise of a cycling slide. The result is a pistol with an acoustic signature of 22 dB — quieter than a whispered conversation. Sterling-Nakamura designed it for executive protection details who need to neutralize threats in environments where gunfire would cause panic — corporate events, diplomatic functions, crowded transit hubs. The weapon's existence is an open secret in security circles.

Street Custom 'Angry Mary' Aerosol Flamethrower#

The simplest possible flamethrower: a can of commercial aerosol product — hairspray, lubricant, insecticide — duct-taped to a piezoelectric igniter salvaged from a kitchen lighter. The flame produced is a 1-2 meter cone of burning aerosol propellant that lasts until the can is empty, typically 15-30 seconds of continuous fire. The Angry Mary is not sophisticated, not reliable, and not safe for the operator, but it costs almost nothing, requires no skill to build, and will absolutely set things on fire. It is the weapon of absolute desperation and has been in continuous use in GLMZ's lowest tiers for as long as anyone can remember.

Street Custom 'Backfire' Weaponized Exhaust System#

A vehicle-mounted improvised weapon created by modifying a motorcycle or small vehicle's exhaust system to inject raw fuel into the exhaust manifold on command, producing a jet of flame from the tailpipe that extends 3-5 meters behind the vehicle. The modification is simple — a secondary fuel injector spliced into the exhaust pipe with a dashboard trigger — and has become common enough in Tier 1 and 2 vehicle culture that mechanics advertise the conversion openly. It is primarily a pursuit deterrent, used to discourage tailgating vehicles and on-foot pursuers, but the flame output is sufficient to cause severe burns and ignite clothing or fuel leaks.

Street Custom 'Cigarette' Pen Gun#

A single-shot .22 short firearm built into a metal cigarette case, with the barrel disguised as a cigarette extending from the case's opening and the firing mechanism hidden beneath a false bottom. The operator opens the case, removes the 'cigarette,' holds it to their lips as if preparing to smoke, and presses a concealed button that fires the round. The entire sequence mimics the universal gesture of lighting a cigarette — reaching into a pocket, opening a case, raising something to your mouth — making the weapon deployment invisible in any environment where smoking is common.

The Cigarette is a Shelf masterpiece of social camouflage. It exploits the fact that a person holding something to their face while fumbling with a small case looks like every other smoker in GLMZ. The weapon's effective range is measured in inches — the .22 short round from a 30mm barrel has barely enough energy to penetrate skin at 2 meters — but the weapon isn't designed for range. It is designed for the moment when you're standing next to someone, pretending to smoke, and you press the barrel against their body under the guise of a casual gesture.

Production quality ranges from elegant to crude. The best Cigarettes are machined from actual cigarette cases with precision barrel inserts and reliable spring-loaded firing pins. The worst are hammered together from tin and hope. All of them share the same terrifying characteristic: they look like nothing, carried by millions of people, performing a gesture that no one questions.

Street Custom 'Four Horsemen' Pipe Pepperbox#

Four steel pipes welded or taped together in a square cluster, each serving as a barrel for a single shotgun shell. The Four Horsemen fires all four barrels in sequence by rotating a crude striker mechanism — turn, fire, turn, fire — giving the operator four shots before the weapon needs to be completely reloaded by extracting spent shells and inserting new ones. The weapon fires .410 shotshells, the smallest common shotgun ammunition, which is cheap, available, and devastating at the 3-5 meter range where the Four Horsemen is most likely to be used.

The Four Horsemen is the Shelf's answer to volume of fire. Where the Nail Biter gives you one shot, the Horsemen gives you four — enough to clear a room, defend a doorway, or ensure that a missed first shot isn't your last. The weapon is larger and heavier than a Nail Biter, carried in a coat pocket or a bag rather than concealed in a waistband, and its crude construction means accuracy degrades rapidly beyond arm's length. But at arm's length, four .410 shotshells fired in rapid succession are lethal regardless of precision.

Construction quality varies wildly. The best Four Horsemen use welded steel pipe with filed chambers and a machined striker plate. The worst use electrical tape and hope. The weapon's four-barrel design means that a malfunction in one barrel doesn't necessarily prevent the others from firing, providing a crude form of redundancy that single-barrel designs lack.

Street Custom 'Gallows' Recurve Bow#

A handmade recurve bow assembled from salvaged composite materials — typically automotive leaf springs, industrial cable for the string, and scrap polymer for the riser. The Gallows represents the lowest-tech weapon in GLMZ that remains genuinely lethal at range. With no electromagnetic components, no battery, no firmware, and no acoustic signature, it is invisible to every detection system in the city. It is a stick that throws smaller sticks, and in a world of networked surveillance, that simplicity is a superpower.

Gallows bows are built by hand in the Shelf, each one unique, each one reflecting the builder's available materials and skill level. Draw weights range from 20 to 60 kilograms depending on the spring steel used, and accuracy depends entirely on the archer's practice. The arrows are similarly improvised — metal rod shafts with filed points, stabilized with whatever passes for fletching. Despite the crude construction, a Gallows arrow through the throat kills as effectively as any precision-manufactured projectile.

The bow has become a symbol of Shelf resistance culture — a weapon that the surveillance state literally cannot see. No electronics to detect, no chemical propellant to sniff, no electromagnetic signature to track. A person with a Gallows bow and sufficient skill can kill from rooftop distance and leave no forensic trace that any automated system can process. The kill has to be investigated by humans, and there aren't enough investigators to cover the Shelf.

Street Custom 'Ghost' Printed Pistol#

A 3D-printed single-shot pistol manufactured on consumer-grade fabrication equipment using freely available design files. The Ghost is produced from high-temperature polymer with a printed barrel, frame, and firing mechanism — the only non-printed component is a short steel barrel liner pressed into the polymer bore and a hardware-store nail for the firing pin. The weapon fires a single 9mm round with enough accuracy and reliability to function as a lethal tool at ranges under 5 meters.

Ghost pistols exist because fabrication technology has made weapons manufacturing a file-sharing problem. The design files circulate on encrypted networks, updated regularly by anonymous engineers who refine the geometry based on field reports and failure analysis. Version 14 — the current standard — has a reliable firing rate of approximately 90% and a barrel life of 8-12 rounds before the steel liner shifts in the polymer housing and accuracy becomes dangerously unpredictable.

The Ghost's most dangerous characteristic is its near-invisibility to standard screening. The polymer frame contains no metal except the barrel liner and firing pin — two small pieces that can be disguised as belt buckle components or hair accessories during separate passage through screening. The weapon can be assembled in 30 seconds from seemingly innocuous parts, fired, and discarded. A Ghost pistol that has been used in a crime looks identical to random polymer debris in a waste container. It is a weapon designed to exist for exactly as long as it is needed and then cease to exist.

This has created a constant arms race between screening technology and printing innovation, with each new detection method met by a new design that evades it. The Ghost's name is apt: it appears, kills, and vanishes.

Street Custom 'Gutterfish' Improvised Speargun#

A crude speargun assembled from PVC pipe, surgical tubing, and sharpened rebar, used by Shelf residents who work, hide, or fight in GLMZ's flooded lower levels. The Gutterfish operates on simple elastic propulsion — the surgical tubing is stretched to store energy, the rebar spear is seated in the PVC barrel, and releasing the retention clip fires the spear at velocities sufficient to penetrate flesh and light materials at ranges up to 5 meters underwater.

Gutterfish spearguns exist because the people who need underwater weapons the most are the ones who can least afford them. The Shelf's lowest levels flood regularly, and residents who refuse to evacuate — because they have nowhere to go, or because leaving means losing what little they own — need tools that work in water. The Gutterfish serves as weapon, fishing tool, and utility device. The same instrument that defends a flooded home also catches the fish that increasingly colonize GLMZ's submerged spaces, providing protein to communities that can't afford the vertical farm produce sold in upper-tier markets.

Every Gutterfish is handmade and unreliable. The surgical tubing degrades in contaminated water, the PVC cracks in cold temperatures, and the rebar spears are never straight enough for consistent accuracy. But the weapon costs Φ10 in materials and can be built by anyone with basic tools, making it the most democratic weapon in GLMZ's flooded underworld.

Street Custom 'Last Word' Ring Gun#

A single-shot firearm built into an oversized ring worn on the index or middle finger, firing a .22 short round from a barrel concealed within the ring's decorative setting. The weapon is activated by pressing the palm-side trigger plate with the thumb while the hand is clenched into a fist. The round fires forward from the ring face, roughly aligned with a pointing gesture. Accuracy is nonexistent beyond 2 meters, but at contact range — pressed against a target's body during a handshake, an embrace, or a struggle — the weapon is lethal.

Last Word rings are handmade in the Shelf by jeweler-gunsmiths who have combined their crafts into a single, desperate art form. Each ring is unique, built around whatever firing mechanism and barrel stock the maker can acquire. The external appearance ranges from crude metal bands to surprisingly sophisticated designs that mimic legitimate jewelry. The best makers produce rings that pass casual inspection, with firing mechanisms hidden behind gemstone settings that swivel aside to reveal the barrel.

The weapon has a grim reputation because of the circumstances of its use. Nobody carries a ring gun as a primary weapon. It is the weapon you carry when you expect to be searched, expect to be held at gunpoint, and expect that the only chance you'll get is when someone comes close enough to touch. It is named the Last Word because it is intended to be used when every other option has been exhausted.

Street Custom 'Loudmouth' Slam-Fire Shotgun#

A two-piece slam-fire shotgun consisting of a barrel pipe and a receiver pipe — the barrel slides into the receiver, and slamming the barrel backward drives the shell onto a fixed firing pin, discharging the round. The Loudmouth fires 12-gauge shotshells without any trigger, safety, or mechanical complexity — the firing mechanism is the operator's arm slamming two pipes together. Reload is performed by sliding the barrel forward, extracting the spent shell, inserting a new one, and slamming again.

The Loudmouth is the most powerful weapon that can be built with zero skill and near-zero materials. Two pipes of the right diameter, a bolt for a firing pin, and an endcap welded or threaded onto the receiver pipe. Total cost: Φ8. Total engineering: none. The weapon fires full-power 12-gauge ammunition — buckshot, slug, whatever the operator can acquire — with all the authority that implies. At 5 meters, a 12-gauge buckshot round from a Loudmouth is identical in lethality to a round from a Φ3,000 combat shotgun.

The weapon's slam-fire mechanism means there is no trigger discipline — the round fires when the operator pushes the barrel home, and the timing of that push is affected by adrenaline, fear, and the chaos of whatever situation requires a pipe shotgun. Accidental discharges are common. The weapon has no safety because there is nothing to put a safety on. It is a pipe that converts forward motion into a dead person.

Street Custom 'Nail Biter' Pipe Pistol#

A single-shot pistol made from a short length of steel pipe, a nail for a firing pin, and a rubber-band-powered striker mechanism. The Nail Biter fires a single .22 or .25 caliber round from a barrel that may or may not be straight, through a chamber that may or may not seal properly, using a firing pin that may or may not strike the primer centered. The weapon represents the absolute minimum viable firearm — the least amount of material and engineering required to make a thing that shoots a bullet.

Nail Biters are the most common weapon in the Shelf, produced in quantities that no tracking system can quantify. The materials cost less than Φ5, the assembly requires no tools beyond a file and pliers, and the instructions have been passed through the community for generations. Every teenager in the Shelf knows how to build one. Most of them have built one. The quality varies from functional to suicidal — some Nail Biters will fire reliably for fifty rounds, while others will blow apart on the first shot.

The weapon's single-round capacity is its defining tactical limitation and its cultural significance. A Nail Biter gives you one shot. One chance to solve whatever problem requires a bullet. This makes every trigger pull a deliberate choice — you can't spray and pray with a weapon that needs to be reloaded by unscrewing the barrel and inserting another round. Nail Biter violence in the Shelf is almost always intentional, personal, and close-range.

The Rat King pattern originated in Tier 1 gang warfare and has spread through fabrication networks.

Despite its crude appearance, the weapon is brutally effective: the rebar spikes concentrate impact force into small areas, defeating soft armor through penetration rather than blunt force, and the heavy steel construction makes each swing potentially lethal.

Street Custom 'Rosary' Bead Garrote#

A garrote wire concealed within a string of decorative beads worn as a bracelet or necklace. The beads are machined from tungsten carbide and threaded on a 1mm monofilament wire with breaking strength of 400 kilograms. When deployed — unclasped and drawn taut between two hands — the wire cuts through unprotected tissue in seconds, and the tungsten beads provide grip points that prevent the wire from slipping through the operator's hands.

Rosary garrotes are Shelf craft — assembled by hand from industrial monofilament and machined beads, then disguised as costume jewelry. They are worn openly, passed through security checkpoints without comment, and carried in environments where no other weapon could enter. The Rosary exploits the most fundamental assumption of weapons screening: jewelry is not dangerous.

The weapon requires close physical contact and significant upper-body strength to deploy effectively, limiting its use to ambush or grapple scenarios. But its concealability is unmatched — a Rosary looks like a piece of inexpensive jewelry, weighs almost nothing, and shows up on X-ray as exactly what it appears to be: a string of metal beads. Only someone who recognizes the specific bead material and wire type would identify it as a weapon, and that requires expertise that most security personnel do not possess.

Street Custom 'Thumper' Improvised Launcher#

A crude single-shot launcher assembled from plumbing pipe, a shotgun firing mechanism, and whatever propellant the builder could acquire. The Thumper fires improvised projectiles — typically tin cans filled with scrap metal and a detonator, or repurposed commercial firework motors with fragmentation sleeves — at ranges between 20 and 100 meters with accuracy best described as 'in that general direction.' The weapon is dangerous to the user nearly as much as the target, with a failure rate that discourages repeat engagements.

Thumpers appear throughout the Shelf whenever tensions escalate to the point where residents feel the need for area weapons. They are built in garages and basements from materials that cost less than Φ50, and their improvised munitions are assembled from similarly available components. The weapons are terrifyingly effective despite their crudeness — an explosion doesn't need to be precise to be lethal, and a can full of scrap metal detonating in a crowded space achieves the same result as military fragmentation at a fraction of the cost.

Every Thumper is unique. There are no production standards, no quality control, and no two weapons that fire the same way. Operators learn their weapon's specific quirks through practice — how far left it pulls, how much the propellant charge varies between shots, whether this particular pipe has a weak seam that might split on the fourth firing. Using a Thumper is an act of faith.

Street Custom 'Tombstone' Concrete Block Launcher#

A pneumatic launcher constructed from salvaged compressed air tanks and steel pipe that fires concrete blocks, bricks, or similarly sized debris at lethal velocity. The Tombstone uses a burst of compressed air to accelerate a rough projectile through a wide-bore barrel, achieving enough velocity to shatter bone and demolish light barriers at close range. Despite every possible disadvantage, the Tombstone fills a niche in Tier 1 warfare: it uses ammunition that is literally everywhere, and the impact of a 2-kilogram concrete block at 50 m/s is not something that body armor is designed to handle.

Street-Custom Gutter Katana 'Flatline'#

A katana-length blade assembled from industrial waste materials — carbon-lattice offcuts from manufacturing, reclaimed structural composite, and scavenged handle wrapping. The Gutter Katana is not a product; it is a phenomenon. Across GLMZ's lower tiers, self-taught bladesmiths produce these weapons from whatever materials are available, and the results range from barely functional clubs to genuinely dangerous cutting weapons that rival corporate products.

The Flatline designation refers to a specific lineage of Gutter Katanas produced in the Undercroft district, where a network of anonymous smiths has developed a technique for heat-treating carbon-lattice offcuts that produces a blade of surprising quality. The process is passed from maker to maker without formal instruction — you learn by watching, and you prove your skill by producing a blade that passes a cutting test against a standardized target. Flatline blades are marked with a simple horizontal line etched near the guard.

The weapon represents the lower tiers' refusal to be disarmed by economics. Corporate weapons cost what lower-tier residents earn in months; a Flatline costs scavenging time and skill. The quality varies, but the cultural statement is consistent: access to violence is not a privilege reserved for those who can afford Crucible's price tags.

Street-Custom Loaded Pipe 'Bell Ringer'#

A length of industrial pipe — typically 40-60 centimeters — filled with lead shot or concrete and capped at both ends. The Bell Ringer is the lower tiers' most common impact weapon: free to manufacture, devastating on impact, and requiring no skill beyond the ability to swing. The loaded pipe's weight (typically 2-4 kilograms depending on fill material and length) generates enormous kinetic energy in even casual swings, and the cylindrical contact surface distributes force across a wide area that defeats the shock-absorbing properties of most light armor.

The weapon's ubiquity in GLMZ's lower tiers has given it a cultural significance that transcends its crude construction. A loaded pipe is not a weapon of choice — it is a weapon of circumstance, carried by people who cannot afford anything better and who have learned that industrial plumbing components are both free and lethal. The distinctive sound of a pipe connecting with a hard surface — a hollow, resonant ring that has earned the weapon its name — is one of the lower tiers' characteristic sounds of violence.

Some lower-tier artisans have elevated the Bell Ringer into something approaching craft, wrapping handles in salvaged leather, adding wrist loops for retention, and selecting specific pipe gauges for optimal weight-to-length ratios. These improved versions are sold or traded within community networks, blurring the line between improvised weapon and purpose-built tool of violence.

Street-Custom Memory Alloy Butterfly Knife 'Quicksilver'#

A butterfly knife (balisong) constructed entirely from shape-memory alloy, allowing the blade and handles to flex, deform, and recover their geometry through rapid manipulation. The Quicksilver takes the traditional balisong — already one of the most dynamic manual weapons in existence — and adds the shape-memory property that allows the blade to deform around obstacles and snap back to cutting rigidity faster than the eye can follow.

Street-level bladesmiths in GLMZ's Filipino diaspora community developed the Quicksilver by adapting industrial shape-memory alloy stock to traditional balisong proportions. The manufacturing process is closely guarded within the community, and production is limited to a handful of smiths who learned the technique from its originator — a retired metalworker named Dante Villanueva-Obi who combined his industrial materials knowledge with his grandmother's balisong traditions.

The weapon's manipulation characteristics are unique — the shape-memory handles flow through the user's fingers with less resistance than conventional steel, enabling manipulation speeds that blur the boundary between weapon handling and sleight of hand. Expert Quicksilver users can open, close, and transition the knife through positions so rapidly that observers cannot determine whether the blade is deployed or stowed at any given moment. This ambiguity is itself a tactical advantage.

A user can have the blade open and cutting before an observer registers the threat, and the shape-memory property means the blade recovers from impacts and deflections that would render a conventional balisong inoperable. The weapon's small size limits it to close-quarters and grappling range, but within that range, the manipulation speed and deformation recovery make it exceptionally difficult to disarm or disable.
cultural context The Quicksilver is a cultural artifact of GLMZ's Filipino diaspora — a community that maintained balisong traditions across generations of displacement and mixing. The weapon's development by a retired metalworker using industrial materials embodies the diaspora's pattern of adapting traditional practices to available resources. The community's protectiveness of the manufacturing process reflects both practical concerns (limiting supply maintains quality and value) and cultural ones (the technique belongs to the community, not to corporate replication).
known users
  • Filipino diaspora martial practitioners
  • Traditional balisong artists
  • Close-quarters specialists with community connections
story hooks
  • Dante Villanueva-Obi has died, and his manufacturing notes are missing. Three of his students each claim to have the complete technique, but each produces slightly different blades. The community must determine which version is the authentic continuation — or whether all three are needed.

The community is divided between those who want to fight the appropriation and those who see wider availability as a form of cultural victory.

Street-Custom Razorwire Wraps 'Glass Hands'#

Strips of industrial razorwire wrapped around padded hand guards — a lower-tier fighting weapon that transforms every punch, grab, and palm strike into a cutting attack. Glass Hands are crude, dangerous to the wearer if improperly constructed, and devastatingly effective in the close-quarters grappling that characterizes lower-tier violence. The razorwire is typically salvaged from perimeter security installations and wound around hand-shaped frames made from molded industrial foam.

The weapon's effectiveness comes from its contact versatility — unlike a blade, which cuts in one direction along one edge, razorwire wraps present cutting surfaces on every surface of the hand. Punches cut. Grabs cut. Blocks cut the attacker. Even a glancing touch draws blood. In grappling situations, an opponent wrestling with someone wearing Glass Hands discovers that every point of contact becomes a wound. The psychological effect of being cut on every surface that touches the fighter is often more decisive than the physical damage.

The risk to the wearer is genuine. Poorly constructed Glass Hands shift during use, exposing the wearer's own skin to the razorwire. Lower-tier fighters accept this risk as the cost of an effective weapon, and experienced users bear characteristic scars on their hands and forearms from construction, training, and combat. These scars have become markers of Glass Hands experience — a visible résumé of lower-tier fighting capability.

Street-Custom Rebar Shiv 'Tetanus Kiss'#

A crude but effective stabbing weapon made from construction rebar ground to a point and wrapped in salvaged grip tape. The Tetanus Kiss is not a designed weapon — it is what happens when someone who cannot afford a Φ50 knife takes a piece of structural steel and makes it dangerous. The rebar's corrugated surface tears rather than cuts, creating ragged wounds that are extremely difficult to close and prone to infection.

The weapon's street name reflects its most feared characteristic: lower-tier medical facilities treat rebar puncture wounds with a specific dread, because the corrugated steel surface drags environmental contaminants — rust, concrete dust, biological matter — deep into the wound channel. Without immediate antimicrobial treatment, infection rates approach 80%. In GLMZ's lower tiers, where medical access is intermittent and expensive, a rebar puncture can kill through sepsis days after the initial injury.

The Tetanus Kiss exists because poverty is a weapon that creates weapons. Every piece of rebar in GLMZ's lower tiers is a potential armament, requiring only motivation and a grinding wheel to transform. Security forces who patrol lower-tier corridors have learned that confiscating improvised weapons is futile — the raw materials are literally the walls and floors.

Subacoustic Vestibular Collapse Drone SVCD-1 'Tilt'#

The SVCD-1 is a compact, agile drone platform built around a single, highly specialized function: the generation of precisely calibrated subacoustic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequencies of the human vestibular system. Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's non-lethal compliance division, the drone produces infrasound pulses in the 0.5–4 Hz range directed through a focused parabolic emitter array at its ventral surface. When these waveforms intersect with a target's inner ear structures, they induce a rapid and total loss of spatial orientation — targets cannot determine up from down, cannot maintain balance, and experience severe nausea within seconds of sustained exposure.

The SVCD-1's engineering challenge was directionality: infrasound at these frequencies is notoriously difficult to focus, and early prototypes affected entire rooms rather than individual targets. TESSERA's solution was a multi-emitter phased array system that uses destructive interference to cancel the waveform outside a narrow 15-degree cone, concentrating the full effect on a single target while leaving adjacent individuals largely unaffected. The system requires continuous tracking to maintain this cone alignment, which is handled by the drone's onboard inertial targeting processor — a TESSERA proprietary unit derived from their precision manufacturing alignment systems.

Beyond immediate incapacitation, repeated or prolonged exposure has been documented to cause lasting vestibular sensitization, where affected individuals experience spontaneous vertigo episodes for weeks afterward when exposed to ordinary low-frequency vibration — engines, heavy machinery, certain music. This residual effect is not listed in TESSERA's official product documentation.

Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge#

The Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge is a directional breaching charge that combines a shaped piezoelectric detonation wave with a tightly collimated acoustic frequency package tuned to cerebrospinal fluid resonance. When placed against a surface — wall, vehicle hull, or floor — the SSDC-4's primary piezoelectric initiator fires a shockwave through the intervening material at a frequency calculated to couple maximally with the subarachnoid space of anyone on the opposite side within a 2-meter radius. The result is traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage without structural breach of the barrier itself.

The charge was originally developed as a counter-hostage tool — a way to neutralize armed individuals behind cover without compromising the structural integrity needed for building clearance. The engineering insight was brutal in its elegance: the wall doesn't need to break if the person behind it does. SSDC-4 units are calibrated with an onboard micro-processor that reads surface material density and adjusts detonation profile to maintain resonance coupling across concrete, composite alloy, and reinforced polymer.

Operators call it 'The White Flash' because survivors — those at the edge of the effective radius — report a blinding white visual event with no accompanying sound, followed by hours of confusion and vomiting. Those at the center of the cone are found in what breach teams describe as 'the quiet position': seated, slumped, or standing still, with no visible wounds and no capacity for coherent response.

Subdermal Current Lance SCL-1 'Needlepoint'#

The SCL-1 is a slender penetrating weapon — functionally a reinforced spike 22cm in length — constructed from a non-conductive ceramic composite sheath over a tungsten-alloy core that serves as an electrode. Upon penetration of the target's skin, the weapon delivers a precisely directed electrical current along the insertion channel, propagating through tissue fluid and targeting conductive pathways — nerves, blood vessels, and implant wiring — rather than simply burning the entry point. The result is a deeply internal electrical injury that causes systemic nerve disruption, implant damage, and in sustained contact, cardiac and neurological cascade effects that are diagnostically consistent with medical emergencies rather than assault.

The SCL-1 was developed within LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' research division as a tool for studying in-vivo electrical propagation through augmented tissue — a legitimate research application that was quietly repurposed. The weapon is powered by a slim handle unit that houses a compressed capacitor bank, delivering between one and five joules of current per activation with a charge cycle of approximately 0.4 seconds. The handle is designed to resemble a medical injector at casual inspection, and the ceramic sheath provides no metallic signature under standard scanner profiles.

The weapon's most controversial feature is its documented effectiveness against augmented individuals specifically. Neural implants, subdermal communication arrays, and myoelectric muscle enhancers all provide additional conductive pathways that amplify internal current propagation, meaning the SCL-1 causes significantly greater damage to augmented targets than to unaugmented ones. This inversion of the typical augmentation-as-protection dynamic has made the weapon both feared and sought after in contexts where augmented operatives represent the primary threat.

Subdermal Ferroelectric Shear Projector#

The Subdermal Ferroelectric Shear Projector fires a focused, rapidly alternating ferroelectric field pulse that penetrates the skin and induces mechanical shear stress in ferromagnetic and piezoelectric materials implanted beneath it — specifically the titanium alloy housings, ceramic substrates, and magnetostrictive actuators common in cybernetic implants. The effect on a heavily augmented target is catastrophic: implant housings fracture along stress lines, flexible circuit substrates delaminate, and the physical interface between biological tissue and synthetic components is violently disrupted. On unaugmented targets, the weapon produces a deep bruising sensation and mild muscle spasm, little more.

Subdermal Shear Projector SSP-1 'Faultline'#

The SSP-1 fires a tightly collimated beam of coherent ultrasonic pressure tuned to the acoustic impedance boundary between biological tissue and subdermal cybernetic plating. The physics are precise and brutal: where natural flesh meets implanted metal, ceramic, or polymer substrate, there exists a discontinuity in acoustic resistance. The Faultline's beam propagates harmlessly through either medium in isolation but generates violent shear stress exactly at that interface. The result is not an explosion or a puncture but a tearing — implants are forcibly separated from the tissue anchoring them, causing catastrophic internal injury without any visible external wound for several seconds.

Subharmonic Flechette Launcher SFL-4 'Hornet'#

The SFL-4 fires a tight cluster of 24 steel micro-flechettes from a rotating drum magazine, each flechette coated in a piezoelectric polymer that activates on deceleration within soft tissue. The flechettes themselves are not individually lethal — each is 1.8mm in diameter and 12mm long — but the cluster dispersal pattern, combined with the piezoelectric activation sequence that fires as each dart decelerates, creates a cascading internal disruption effect that is grotesquely effective against unarmored targets. Against light armor, the flechettes lack individual penetrating power, but three or four cluster shots against the same panel can compromise soft armor integrity enough to allow subsequent rounds to penetrate.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's engineering rationale for the piezoelectric coating was ostensibly medical — the activation signature was derived from research into internal tissue stimulation for nerve damage treatment. The SFL-4 was developed under a security applications contract that repurposed this coating for terminal ballistic enhancement. What distinguishes it from conventional flechette weapons is the sequenced disruption cascade: the flechettes do not all activate simultaneously. The deepest-penetrating darts activate first, creating an internal pressure wave that the shallower darts then amplify, producing a disruption effect far larger than the physical volume of the flechettes would suggest.

The weapon's design is deliberately compact — it resembles an oversized semi-automatic pistol with a wide, cylindrical magazine housing — and it is deceptively light for what it does. Operators describe the firing experience as anticlimactic: a soft pneumatic 'pop' and then the target's reaction to 24 piezo-activated micro-darts is rarely anticlimactic at all. The SFL-4 has a disturbing reputation in field medicine; the flechettes are extremely difficult to locate and remove without specialized scanning equipment.

Several medical ethics organizations have campaigned against it specifically — the flechette retrieval problem means that wounded targets who survive the immediate hit face serious long-term health consequences even with prompt medical care. This has made it politically toxic, which in turn has made it attractive to certain operators who specifically want to create complications beyond the immediate engagement. Among street operators, it has a nasty reputation as a weapon used by people who want their targets to suffer.

Subharmonic Thermal Vortex Projector STVP-2 'Millstone'#

The STVP-2 generates a localized thermal vortex by simultaneously projecting two intersecting subharmonic infrared beams at a target point. Where the beams converge, destructive interference between their waveforms produces a rapidly rotating thermal gradient — a spinning column of alternating hot and cool bands that exerts torsional mechanical stress on any matter caught within it. The effect on organic tissue is visceral: the vortex does not burn so much as it wrings, producing deep-tissue trauma analogous to extreme mechanical torsion while leaving the skin surface comparatively intact. Internal hemorrhaging and structural damage to connective tissue are the primary injury mechanisms.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the STVP-2 originally as an industrial tool for non-contact material stress-testing, and the weapon's lineage is visible in its form factor — it resembles a modified survey instrument more than a firearm, with a wide dual-emitter head mounted on a pistol-grip frame and a large rotary dial on the side for adjusting vortex intensity and rotation frequency. The 'Millstone' nickname refers both to this dial and to the grinding quality of the effect on targets. Operators describe the sound of a firing weapon as a low, nauseating hum that is felt more than heard.

The weapon's primary limitation is its fixed effective range of 6–14 meters — the intersecting beams require a minimum distance to converge properly and lose coherence beyond the maximum. This makes the Millstone unsuitable for long-range engagements, but within its optimal band it produces injuries that body armor is largely ineffective against, as the torsional effect penetrates most rigid materials by exploiting their own internal stress fracture lines.

Submersible Cavity Interdiction Drone SCID-2 'Lamprey'#

The SCID-2 is a narrow-profile autonomous drone designed to navigate fluid-filled or flooded infrastructure — drainage systems, cooling pipelines, flooded basements, sewage networks, and submerged tunnel sections. At 34 centimeters in length and 6 centimeters in diameter, the Lamprey moves through pipes and conduits inaccessible to conventional platforms. It is propelled by a peristaltic pump drive that mimics biological fluid movement, producing almost no acoustic signature and no visible wake in slow-moving water. Navigation is handled by a combination of sonar mapping and a pre-loaded infrastructure dataset that Helix Biosystems licenses from municipal engineering contractors.

The Lamprey's primary payload is a hydrostatic pressure charge — a compressed liquid charge that the drone positions against a target surface before detonating. In pipe environments, the blast is directional and catastrophic, capable of rupturing reinforced conduit or breaching basement walls from the waterside. In open flooded environments, the drone can operate as a guided mine, positioning itself beneath a target and detonating on proximity trigger. A secondary payload option replaces the hydrostatic charge with a neurochemical dispersal package, releasing a water-soluble incapacitant into a connected fluid system — a capability that regulatory bodies have flagged as a potential mass-casualty tool.

The Lamprey occupies a unique tactical niche in GLMZ because the city's infrastructure is extensively flooded and interconnected. The lower districts — particularly the Brackwater and Sump neighborhoods — sit atop a vast network of partially submerged tunnels and service corridors that Lamprey units navigate freely. Helix Biosystems markets the SCID-2 as an infrastructure inspection and repair platform with 'optional security configurations,' a framing that regulators have repeatedly challenged without success.

Suborbital Acoustic Relay Drone SARD-1 'Tuning Fork'#

The SARD-1 is a high-altitude loitering drone designed to serve as an acoustic relay node, amplifying and directing subharmonic resonance attacks generated by a ground-based emitter to targets beyond the emitter's direct line-of-sight. Operating at altitudes between 800 and 2,000 meters, the Tuning Fork carries a phased acoustic transducer array that receives a directional subharmonic beam from a paired ground emitter, shifts its phase geometry, and rebroadcasts it downward in a tightly focused cone. The result is precision subharmonic delivery through ceilings, floors, and reinforced structures that would otherwise attenuate or block a ground-level emitter.

The drone's phase-shift architecture is its core technical achievement—conventional acoustic relay systems introduce destructive interference during rebroadcast, dramatically reducing efficacy. The SARD-1 uses a real-time interferometric compensation algorithm developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC to maintain coherent subharmonic output despite the geometry change between receive and transmit angles. This allows operators to deliver resonant structural stress or physiological disruption to targets inside hardened facilities without breaching the structure or alerting occupants to the direction of the attack.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC initially developed the SARD-1 for geological survey work—mapping subterranean infrastructure using directed acoustic pulses—before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS licensed the transducer architecture for weaponized applications. The survey-grade civilian variant still exists and is legally available, creating a persistent gray market where modified survey drones are sold with weapon-grade phase arrays installed by third-party vendors.

Subsonic Caseless Bolt Rifle SCBR-1 'Quiet Ledger'#

The SCBR-1 fires a 12.7mm caseless subsonic round using a precision-engineered linear combustion chamber that burns propellant so completely and at such controlled pressure that the muzzle report is reduced to approximately 118 dB without any suppressor — well below the threshold of conventional recognition as a gunshot. Combined with an integrated wet suppressor that uses a sealed liquid baffle system, the total acoustic signature drops to 94 dB: audible at close range but indistinguishable at distance from mechanical noise, HVAC systems, or street clutter. The caseless ammunition eliminates ejection noise entirely, and the manually-operated rotary bolt produces only the soft mechanical click of cycling. At 200 meters in an urban environment, the weapon is functionally silent.

The SCBR-1 was developed by RINGO CORPONATION's advanced projects division under a research contract originally framed around 'acoustic security assessment tools' — a designation that allowed the project to proceed without triggering weapons development review boards. The weapon's 12.7mm subsonic round was engineered specifically to maintain terminal effectiveness despite reduced velocity: the projectile uses a dense tungsten core with a controlled-deformation polymer jacket that produces consistent expansion at subsonic speeds, maintaining wound ballistics comparable to a standard supersonic 7.62mm round. The trade-off is range — effective precision fire is limited to approximately 300 meters, beyond which the heavy subsonic projectile drops steeply.

The weapon's name comes from its role in RINGO CORPONATION's internal mythology as the instrument of quiet corporate accounting — the settling of debts that cannot be settled openly. It is a precision rifle in the traditional sense, manually cycled, requiring a shooter who understands patience and positioning. The wet suppressor requires replacement of the liquid baffle cartridge every 30 shots, and the caseless ammunition is proprietary to RINGO's supply chain, meaning operators must maintain a relationship with RINGO's logistics network to stay armed.

Subsonic Cavity Charge#

The SCC-9 is a proximity-triggered area-denial charge that functions not through fragmentation or overpressure but through the generation of precisely tuned subsonic acoustic pulses at the moment of detonation. Rather than a single explosive event, the SCC-9 produces a rapid sequence of 14 discrete pressure pulses within a 200-millisecond window, each calibrated to a frequency between 7Hz and 19Hz — the range most effective at inducing resonance in human thoracic and abdominal cavities. The result is severe internal trauma, disorientation, nausea, and in close proximity, rupture of air-filled organs without external visible injury.

The charge body contains a layered piezoelectric pulse generator surrounding a small conventional explosive core. The explosive initiates the sequence, but the piezoelectric stack shapes and amplifies the output waveform, converting raw blast energy into the structured subsonic pulse train. This conversion is approximately 60% efficient, meaning the SCC-9 produces significantly less structural damage than a comparable conventional charge — walls remain intact, infrastructure is undamaged — while maximizing biological effect. ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the underlying pulse architecture for industrial vibration dampening before the application was weaponized.

The SCC-9 is triggered by a passive acoustic sensor that detects footfall vibration, making it one of the few charges in GLMZ's black market that cannot be defeated by optical or thermal countermeasures. It is also extraordinarily difficult to detect passively — it emits no EM signature, no chemical trace, and its housing is ceramic composite that defeats standard metal detection. Clearance teams in the city's lower tiers have learned to treat any unidentified object on a floor as a potential SCC-9.

Swarm Dielectric Dispersal Node SDDN-3 'Locust'#

The SDDN-3 deploys a cloud of 400–600 semi-autonomous micro-drones, each no larger than a thumbnail, that distribute themselves across a designated target zone and simultaneously discharge stored dielectric energy into any conductive surface they contact. Each node carries a capacitor array charged via inductive relay from the launch canister, allowing the swarm to sustain its dispersal pattern for up to 90 seconds before terminal discharge. The drones navigate using a low-latency mesh protocol, redistributing around obstacles and reforming after partial neutralization.

What distinguishes the SDDN-3 from conventional area-denial systems is its adaptive saturation logic. If a portion of the swarm is disrupted by EMP countermeasures or physical interference, surviving nodes reassign coverage zones in under 200 milliseconds, ensuring no gap in the dielectric envelope. Targets within the zone experience cascading surface charge buildup across armor, cybernetics, and exposed skin simultaneously, causing localized dielectric breakdown in synthetic materials and severe muscular disruption in unshielded organics.

Originally developed for infrastructure security—specifically to disable unauthorized drones encroaching on TESSERA CORPONATION server campuses—the SDDN-3 was rapidly adopted by paramilitary contractors after field operators discovered its effectiveness against augmented combatants. The swarm's characteristic low hum before dispersal has given it a grim nickname on the streets of GLMZ's industrial districts.

TESSERA CORPONATION's original marketing positioned the weapon as a 'precision area-denial solution,' but its reputation on the street tells a different story. Mid-tier fixers who can afford the restricted license use SDDN-3 canisters as a status marker, displaying spent housings on their workspace walls. Scavengers prize dead nodes for their miniature capacitor arrays, which have a thriving secondary market in DIY electronics.

Synaptic Drift Emitter SDE-4 'Lullaby'#

The Synaptic Drift Emitter SDE-4 operates by broadcasting a precisely tuned electromagnetic envelope that interferes with the brain's default mode network — the cluster of regions responsible for maintaining baseline conscious orientation. Rather than inducing unconsciousness directly, it causes a cascading desynchronization of thalamic relay signals, producing a state of dissociative fugue in which targets remain physically mobile but mentally absent, wandering without volition or coherent threat response. The effect is reversible within minutes of exposure ending, leaving no detectable tissue damage.

What makes the SDE-4 distinctive is its selectivity algorithm, developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's neurological warfare division after seven years of contested research. The emitter can be calibrated to exclude individuals wearing certified neural dampeners or TESSERA-standard cortical implants, allowing operators to move through a drifted crowd unaffected. This selective broadcast footprint earned it the nickname 'Lullaby' — it puts everyone else to sleep while leaving the user wide awake.

In practice the weapon has a distinctive soft hum at 14 Hz, just below the threshold of conscious hearing, which experienced targets have learned to associate with sudden dissociation. Veteran soldiers operating in zones where SDE-4s are known to be deployed sometimes describe a Pavlovian dread response to low ambient drone sounds — a psychological legacy that persists long after exposure.

Synaptic Overload Gauntlet SOG-3 'Seizure'#

The SOG-3 is a full-hand combat gauntlet housing a dense array of transcranial magnetic stimulation coils embedded in the palm and finger assemblies. On contact with a target's skull or upper cervical spine, the gauntlet delivers a precisely timed sequence of high-intensity magnetic pulses that induce involuntary neural firing across multiple cortical regions simultaneously. The result is immediate and total motor control disruption — a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that renders the target non-functional for twelve to forty seconds, followed by a period of profound disorientation lasting several minutes.

The SOG-3's engineering challenge was achieving sufficient field strength for reliable neural induction while maintaining a chassis light enough for combat use. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's solution was a laminated coil architecture using superconductive filament wound at near-molecular density, powered by a forearm-mounted burst capacitor that delivers the full charge in a 0.08-second pulse. The gauntlet requires skin or thin-material contact to function reliably — heavy helmets and full cranial shielding significantly reduce effectiveness, though even partial contact with an unshielded neck produces measurable impairment.

A secondary effect, noted in field reports but absent from official documentation, is the gauntlet's interaction with neural implants. Targets with cognitive augmentations — memory chips, neural co-processors, reflex accelerators — frequently experience device corruption or complete burnout alongside the induced seizure. This has made the SOG-3 particularly feared in circles where neural augmentation is common, as the loss of a high-grade cognitive implant can be professionally and financially devastating beyond the immediate physical harm.

Talon Systems Grav-Pulse Emitter GPE-3 'Downdraft'#

A directed gravitational weapon that projects a focused pulse of gravitational force in a cone-shaped area of effect. Unlike the localized gravity wells of the GL-3 Crush Depth, the Downdraft produces a broad directional push — effectively a gravitational shockwave that slams everything in its path to the ground with 8-12G of downward force for approximately 0.5 seconds.

Talon Systems developed the GPE-3 as a non-lethal crowd control weapon that exploits gravitational manipulation at lower intensities than Arcturus's lethal GL-3. The Downdraft's pulse is calibrated to incapacitate rather than kill — the brief duration prevents the sustained compression that causes organ failure, while the force magnitude is sufficient to drop even augmented targets to the ground and prevent them from rising for several seconds.

The weapon's cone-shaped area of effect covers a 15-meter wide swath at maximum range, making it effective against groups of targets. The gravitational pulse passes through cover and concealment — walls, furniture, and vehicles provide no protection against a force that acts on mass itself.

The Raptor's BCI integration includes an inertial navigation system that calculates firing solutions based on the shooter's velocity, acceleration, and angular rate. It allows precision engagement during maneuvers that would make conventional aim impossible.

Tectonic Shear Gauntlet#

The Tectonic Shear Gauntlet is a powered combat gauntlet developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions for close-quarters urban pacification operations. Embedded within its reinforced knuckle array are sixteen independently actuated piezoelectric transducer nodes, each capable of generating a localized shear wave pulse timed to the moment of impact. When the fist connects with a surface — biological or structural — the system fires a cascading lateral stress fracture pattern into the target, multiplying the destructive potential of a single strike by propagating internal rupture along natural material fault lines rather than relying on raw kinetic energy alone.

What distinguishes the TSG-4 from simpler shock gauntlets is its onboard Fault Mapping Processor, a compact subsystem that reads surface impedance data through the fingertip contact pads during the half-second before a committed strike. This allows the weapon to modulate its shear frequency in real time — hardened ceramics, bone, composite armor, and biological tissue all receive individually tuned pulses optimized to their structural resonance. The result is a weapon that hits differently depending on what it hits, adapting like a surgeon's understanding of material science applied through a closed fist.

The gauntlet's external profile is deliberately understated: matte-black articulated plating over a gel-damping inner glove, with no visible emitters or power cells. Operators have noted that its subtlety is part of its psychological value — adversaries rarely recognize the weapon until after the first strike has already shattered something internal.

Tessellated Optical Denial Drone TODD-2 'Blindspot'#

The TODD-2 operates as a swarm-capable photonic denial platform — each individual unit is a flat hexagonal tile roughly 12 cm across, housing a phased array of micro-lensed emitters that produce precisely sculpted coherent light interference patterns. When a single unit detects a target via thermal or motion signature, it positions itself in the subject's visual cone and activates its pattern array, producing a persistent false-geometry overlay in the target's visual field — not blindness, but a convincing spatial hallucination that makes distances, edges, and surfaces unreliable. Targets frequently walk into walls, misjudge step heights, or freeze entirely trying to parse contradictory spatial data.

The TODD-2's genuine tactical edge emerges when multiple units coordinate. Three or more tiles triangulating a single target can produce a full 270-degree interference envelope, effectively trapping the target in a bubble of fabricated geometry. Operators describe the effect as 'putting someone inside a painting.' The swarm communicates via low-power mesh radio with negligible emissions signature, making electronic detection difficult. VANTABLACK MEDIA's involvement in its development is rarely advertised but evident in the emitter array's lineage — it borrows heavily from their immersive architectural projection systems.

The tiles are fragile by drone standards and were never designed for contested airspace. They perform poorly in rain and fail entirely in direct high-lumen environments. Their power cells last approximately 40 minutes at full interference output, after which they return to a designated recovery point or drop to the ground inert.

Tessera Adaptive Marksman Platform TAMP-5 'Mimic'#

The TAMP-5 Mimic is a DMR with onboard AI that studies enemy marksmen's firing patterns and develops countermeasures in real-time. When engaged against an opposing designated marksman, the Mimic's AI analyzes incoming fire to determine the enemy's weapon type, estimated position, firing rhythm, and engagement tendencies. This analysis is presented to the operator as a BCI overlay showing the predicted timing and direction of the enemy's next shot.

The rifle fires 6.5mm caseless through a precision barrel and features a multi-sensor suite that detects incoming projectile signatures — supersonic crack analysis, ballistic trajectory backtracking, and thermal flash detection combine to build a model of the opposing shooter. The system improves with each exchanged shot, becoming more accurate in its predictions as the engagement continues.

Tessera markets the Mimic at Φ19,000 as a counter-sniper platform for designated marksmen who expect to face skilled opposition. The AI's ability to predict an enemy marksman's behavior creates an asymmetric advantage — the Mimic operator knows when and where the next shot is coming, while their opponent operates blind. In marksman-vs-marksman engagements, this information advantage is often decisive.

Tessera Adaptive Platform TAP-5 'Chameleon'#

The TAP-5 Chameleon is Tessera's modular assault platform, designed to reconfigure between three operational modes without tools. The weapon's core receiver accepts barrel, stock, and feed assemblies that snap-lock into position, allowing an operator to convert from a compact 5.56mm carbine to a 7.62mm battle rifle to a 4.6mm high-velocity PDW configuration in under thirty seconds.

Each configuration carries its own ballistic profile in the weapon's onboard computer, and the BCI smart-link automatically adjusts aim-assist parameters when the operator swaps modules. Tessera sells the TAP-5 as a system — the base receiver plus three conversion kits runs Φ12,000, but the logistics savings of carrying one weapon platform instead of three justify the cost for extended operations.

The Chameleon's weakness is the mechanical complexity of its quick-change system. Each locking interface is a potential failure point, and field conditions can foul the snap-lock mechanisms. Operators who trust the TAP-5 maintain it religiously. Those who don't carry a backup.

Tessera Attrition Engine TE-9 'Patience'#

A semi-autonomous emplaced weapon system designed for siege warfare. The Attrition Engine fires 8mm caseless rounds at a controlled 200 RPM — deliberately slow compared to conventional support weapons — but is designed to maintain this rate for days without interruption, attended only by periodic ammunition resupply.

Tessera designed the Patience for corporate territorial disputes that play out over weeks rather than hours. The weapon's fire rate is calculated to produce maximum psychological attrition with minimum ammunition expenditure. The TE-9's targeting AI engages targets of opportunity at unpredictable intervals, denying sleep, movement, and resupply to enemy positions through the constant threat of precisely-placed suppressive fire.

The Attrition Engine is mounted on a self-leveling platform with a 360-degree rotation capability. Its sensor suite tracks movement within its engagement zone and fires at calculated intervals designed to be psychologically unpredictable — sometimes seconds apart, sometimes hours, ensuring that no pattern can be identified and no safe window can be predicted.

Tessera Autonomous Marksman Platform TAMP-2 'Arbiter'#

The TAMP-2 Arbiter is a DMR designed to operate semi-autonomously from a fixed position. The weapon can be deployed on a stabilized tripod mount with its own sensor suite, power supply, and targeting AI, functioning as an unmanned precision overwatch platform. A remote operator provides engagement authorization through BCI link, but the weapon handles target detection, tracking, and firing solution calculation independently.

The Arbiter fires 7mm caseless from a precision barrel with an automated round-chambering system that maintains the weapon's readiness without human intervention. The sensor suite includes visual, thermal, and millimeter-wave radar that provides all-weather target detection at ranges exceeding the weapon's effective firing distance. The AI prioritizes targets based on threat assessment algorithms that can be pre-configured for specific operational parameters.

Tessera sells the TAMP-2 at Φ45,000 per unit as a force multiplier for precision overwatch. A single remote operator can manage up to four Arbiters simultaneously, providing coverage that would require four human marksmen in four separate positions. The weapon's autonomous capabilities raise the same ethical concerns as all autonomous weapons — the AI identifies and tracks targets, but a human must authorize each engagement. The authorization delay is measured in milliseconds, raising questions about how meaningful that human oversight really is.

Tessera Autonomous Rifle Platform TARP-3 'Delegate'#

The TARP-3 Delegate is an assault rifle designed to be wielded by humanoid combat drones rather than human operators. Tessera engineered every aspect of the weapon for machine operation — the grip pressure requirements exceed human hand strength, the trigger pull weight is set at 15 kilograms, and the manual of arms requires motor precision that only servos can deliver. A human can physically carry the Delegate but cannot effectively operate it.

The weapon fires 6mm caseless through a conventional gas system, but its fire-control is entirely machine-mediated. A hardened data port replaces the BCI link, connecting directly to the combat drone's targeting system. The Delegate achieves consistent sub-half-MOA accuracy at all ranges because the platform holding it does not breathe, flinch, or fatigue. Rate of fire is limited by the weapon's cyclic rate rather than the operator's trigger finger.

Tessera sells the TARP-3 exclusively as part of complete drone weapon systems, bundled with their combat automata. The weapon is useless without a drone, and the drone is less effective without its purpose-built weapon. This interdependency is deliberate — Tessera wants to sell platforms, not components.

TESSERA CB-5 'Viper Strike'#

A compact repeating crossbow with an integrated chemical payload injection system. The CB-5 fires short bolts from a 12-bolt gravity-feed magazine, each bolt hollow and loaded with 0.5ml of operator-selected chemical agent that is injected into the wound channel upon impact through a pressure-activated plunger mechanism. The bolt itself causes minimal physical damage — a 4mm puncture wound that might go unnoticed in a chaotic environment. The chemical payload does the killing.

TESSERA supplies the CB-5 with a catalog of approved chemical loadouts: fast-acting paralytic agents for capture operations, delayed-onset neurotoxins for deniable assassination, and incapacitating sedatives for extraction. The weapon's true danger is its versatility — any liquid agent that fits in a 0.5ml reservoir can be loaded, and the underground market has developed payloads that TESSERA never intended: synthetic opioid overdose loads, corrosive agents, and tailored biotoxins designed for specific genetic profiles.

The CB-5 is nearly silent, fires rapidly, and delivers chemical payloads that can kill hours after exposure. It is the preferred weapon for operators who need their target to die somewhere else, at some other time, from what looks like something other than murder.

Tessera Chronos Field Disruptor CFD-1 'Lag Spike'#

A classified experimental weapon that projects a localized temporal distortion field — an area approximately 3 meters in diameter where the passage of time is slowed relative to the surrounding environment. Targets within the field experience subjective time normally, but external observers see them moving at approximately one-tenth normal speed.

Tessera's quantum physics division developed the Chronos Disruptor based on theoretical work suggesting that gravitational manipulation at extreme intensities can produce time dilation effects. The CFD-1 does not stop time — it creates a steep temporal gradient that slows all processes within the field, from chemical reactions to neural signaling to projectile trajectories.

The weapon is Tessera's most classified project, with fewer than five operational units in existence. The temporal distortion field persists for approximately 10 seconds before the quantum effects collapse, and the energy required to maintain even this brief distortion requires a power system that occupies a small vehicle. The man-portable designation is generous — the weapon is backpack-mounted and requires a two-person crew.

TESSERA Corponation Executive Aegis Wand EAW-1 'Silhouette'#

The EAW-1 'Silhouette' is TESSERA's entry into the executive personal defense market — a device so carefully designed to avoid looking like a weapon that it has become the definitive example of what the category can achieve. The Silhouette is a 38-centimeter carbon-fiber rod, 12mm in diameter, with a matte black finish and a single brushed-steel accent ring near the base. In its carrying configuration, it nestles inside a custom-fitted sleeve built into the lining of a compatible TESSERA Executive Series briefcase, or alternatively within the hollow shaft of a TESSERA-branded umbrella accessory sold separately. In either configuration, it passes visual inspection, standard metal detection (the carbon-fiber construction contains no ferrous metal), and even casual physical search by someone who does not know to look for it.

The Silhouette's discharge system is among the most refined available in any sub-military shock device. TESSERA's engineering team spent three development cycles optimizing the contact electrode array — a 4-centimeter active zone at the rod's tip — to deliver a precisely shaped 180,000-volt pulse with a waveform specifically tuned to maximize disruption across the augmentation profiles most common in Tier 4-5 business environments: light BCI systems, cosmetic subdermal implants, and standard executive health-monitoring chrome. A secondary pulse mode, accessible through a second grip press, activates a partial EMP burst that disrupts non-hardened electronics within the 4-centimeter contact zone — sufficient to crash a standard BCI or disable a smartwatch, but calibrated below the full anti-cyberware damage threshold of TESSERA's NSR-1 line.

At Φ8,500, the Silhouette is priced as a luxury item and positioned as one. TESSERA's marketing materials feature it alongside premium accessories and describe it as 'the standard of discreet personal confidence.' It is sold through TESSERA's authorized executive retail network, requiring a standard stun device license and a TESSERA Executive Client registration that, in practice, functions as a social vetting process — TESSERA does not sell the Silhouette to people they deem inconsistent with the brand.
